acceptanceCriteria.text: AC-QB-GATES-ALL-SUCCESSFUL-COMPLETION-PATHS: Successful final-answer payloads/success events remain withheld until required checks pass; blocked or incomplete diagnostics remain deliverable without claiming success. Test successful, correctable-incomplete and infrastructure-blocked outcomes through each final-delivery path. A corrected final attempt uses the same open request and only succeeds after every applicable obligation is verified; unchanged incomplete attempts stop at the existing bounded limit. Infrastructure failure exposes supported recovery without allowing ordinary work or discarding audit evidence. TEST-QB-010: gates_all_successful_completion_paths. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-BLOCKS-COMPLETION-ON-FAILED-MISSING-OR-STALE-VERIFICATION: Code/doc edits and command-made changes invalidate stale evidence; failed/missing applicable checks block completion. The signed policy selects every applicable runner from package ownership and dependency scope, including non-sdk VS Code suites, all distinct desktop runners and required native checks. Evidence binds policy digest and pre/post source fingerprints; changes during verification invalidate it. Ignored receipt churn alone does not invalidate source evidence. Baseline failures, blocked chains and required platform/credential cases remain explicit blockers until resolved or changed by an operator decision. TEST-QB-011: blocks_completion_on_failed_missing_or_stale_verification. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-CLASSIFIES-OPERATIONS-AND-GATES-PHASE-CLOSURE-ON-VERIFIED-HV-RECEIPT: A host-owned classifier derives phaseId and phaseClosing from trusted governed TODO/task mutations and MCP records, never model prose. It classifies operationClass from that trusted state plus source fingerprints: any working-tree content change within the verification-policy scope is development, whether made by an edit tool or command; administrative turns have unchanged source contents and only TODO, requirement or session-record effects. Administrative turns carry no verification or HV obligation; development turns complete only after required verification passes for the current fingerprint; a mutation completing a task or setting done: true on a TODO listed as phase-gated by the signed workspace verification policy is rejected without a valid HV receipt; for this workspace the policy lists QB-AGENT-001 tasks prefixed P1: through P5: and Final:, and done: true on QB-AGENT-001; TODOs without a phase-gate entry carry no HV obligation. The named test rejects forged reviewer/root identities, model-selected phase selectors, partial or missing verdict persistence, absent scores and every sub-98 value without rounding; it accepts valid lexical scores only under the agreed lossless numeric contract. Canonical task readback must match the attempted phase transition and current verified plan/base/head; read failure or mismatch leaves that transition pending. Administrative reconciliation never satisfies a product AC or silently closes a phase. TEST-QB-012: classifies_operations_and_gates_phase_closure_on_verified_hv_receipt (administrative, development, valid receipt, forged receipt, stale receipt). TDD: P1. Valid receipt: read back through the supported plugin from a completed MCP turn whose session agent identity is the configured reviewer identity (ClaudeCode), not the host identity; its stored verdict records OverallVerdict AGREE, accuracy and completeness >=98, and plan hash, base SHA and head SHA equal to the closing state. The host binds model-facing session tools to its own agentIdentity and sessionId; tool arguments cannot set agent, sourceType or sessionId. An administrator or unrestricted user-authorized shell with the raw marker key can bypass the application and forge server records; this on-disk credential bypass is outside the application-level guarantee and is documented as a limit under AC-QB-CHECKS-DOCUMENTED-COMMANDS-DEFAULTS-AND-CONTRACTS.

AC-QB-ISOLATES-ALL-VERIFICATION-PROCESSES-FROM-OPERATOR-APPLICATION-STATE: Every required verification fixture and its child processes use isolated application state and explicitly selected test identities, workspace, discovery endpoints and ports before application initialization. Tests must not read live operator credentials, attach to a live operator hub or change operator application state. Seeded external-state canaries and inventories remain unchanged after success, assertion failure, timeout and cancellation. Cleanup affects only resources owned by that test run. Any intentionally live integration fixture uses an explicitly provisioned test account/workspace and cannot silently inherit the operator account. Read-only compiler/package caches may be shared when they contain no operator application identity or mutable product state. TEST cases: Pre-import environment capture; account feature-flag callback; real HOME inherited by a child; parallel fixtures; wrong discovery file/port; failure and timeout cleanup; mocked negative fixture plus a real compiled positive launch; canaries outside the test root. TEST-QB-071: isolates_all_verification_processes_from_operator_application_state. TDD: P1. Staged regressions: P2, P3, P4, P5.

acceptanceCriteria.text: AC-QB-MAKES-NO-PROHIBITED-CLINE-SERVICE-REQUESTS: Startup/settings/work/resume/reconnect/refresh make zero prohibited Cline Cloud/control/telemetry requests, including with old credentials/caches. Exercise process networking, webview/browser initialization, native updater and background callbacks from fresh and legacy configurations on every shipped host. Seed excluded credentials/caches and prove zero prohibited traffic without deleting or migrating upstream files; permitted direct-provider traffic is distinguishable from prohibited service traffic. TEST-QB-016: makes_no_prohibited_cline_service_requests. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-REJECTS-CLINE-CLOUD-EXECUTION-AND-CONTROL-PATHS: Hosted inference/cloud agents/account dependencies/remote config/feature flags/uploads cannot be re-enabled by settings/fallback. TEST-QB-017: rejects_cline_cloud_execution_and_control_paths. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-RUNS-PERMITTED-EXECUTION-WITHOUT-CLINE-ACCOUNT: Local hub, direct providers, compatible self-controlled remote hosts work without a Cline account. Include positive authenticated direct-provider execution, configured proxy use and compatible hub/remote operation; missing or invalid direct-provider credentials produce an actionable failure, never a Cline account fallback or silent provider substitution. TEST-QB-018: runs_permitted_execution_without_cline_account. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-PREVENTS-LEGACY-ACCOUNT-ONBOARDING-REACTIVATION: Desktop onboarding contains no Cline account sign-in, account-key, hosted recommendation, subscription-upsell or account-backed GitHub activation path. Legacy identity, enabled feature flags and a restored GitHub onboarding step cannot issue account/control requests or select a hosted provider; the operator can configure a direct provider or skip without an invented connection. TEST-QB-061: prevents_legacy_account_onboarding_reactivation. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-OFFERS-ONLY-COMPATIBLE-DIRECT-ONBOARDING-FORMS: A setup form offers only permitted providers whose declared authentication and required configuration it can collect. The desktop key-only form excludes hosted aliases, alternate authentication and mandatory endpoint configuration; supported providers needing those fields remain reachable through Settings. Failed save never advances or selects a fallback; successful explicit selection preserves its provider/model. TEST-QB-062: offers_only_compatible_direct_onboarding_forms. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-SURFACES-SCHEDULE-CATALOG-FAILURE-WITHOUT-FALLBACK: Empty, failed, delayed or disabled desktop schedule catalogs never synthesize an enabled provider or model. Catalog failures expose the error and a Settings recovery action or instruction. Excluded provider aliases are absent even in stale catalog data, and no excluded provider discovery is initiated. TEST-QB-063: surfaces_schedule_catalog_failure_without_fallback. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-PRESERVES-EXPLICIT-SCHEDULE-PROVIDER-MODEL-SELECTION: Schedule creation requires an explicit permitted provider and model, or a previously explicit remembered pair still available in that same provider catalog. Missing provider/model blocks submission with an actionable message and no mutation. Editing or catalog refresh preserves the existing permitted pair, without choosing the first catalog entry or borrowing another provider model. Valid direct create/update preserves that exact pair. TEST-QB-064: preserves_explicit_schedule_provider_model_selection. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-REQUIRES-EXPLICIT-REPLACEMENT-OF-HOSTED-SCHEDULE-SELECTION: Editing a legacy hosted schedule presents an actionable exclusion diagnostic and requires an explicit direct provider/model replacement before saving. Opening, canceling or failed validation neither activates the hosted provider nor silently rewrites the stored schedule. The replacement uses only the operator-selected permitted pair. TEST-QB-065: requires_explicit_replacement_of_hosted_schedule_selection. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-KEEPS-MIGRATED-SCHEDULE-MODEL-SELECTION-ATOMIC: When a schedule contains the structured modelSelection field, its provider/model pair is authoritative as a unit. Missing or malformed members remain incomplete and block saving until explicitly repaired; they never inherit a provider or model from legacy scalar fields. Schedules without the structured field retain their explicit legacy direct pair. Mixed-format and partially migrated records cannot combine identities from different provider selections. TEST-QB-066: keeps_migrated_schedule_model_selection_atomic. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-REQUIRES-EXPLICIT-DIRECT-DESKTOP-RECOVERY: Desktop chat composition and recovery never fetch or subscribe to hosted feature flags, activate hosted execution from legacy state, or offer account-backed recovery links. Hosted-target attempts show an actionable exclusion and leave the selected direct provider/model and stored history unchanged. Moving from an unavailable hosted history session to permitted execution requires an explicit new local or self-controlled remote session; it does not silently reinterpret the old session. Explicit local recovery preserves a permitted captured or remembered provider/model pair, leaves missing selection incomplete for Settings, and never chooses a hosted or first-catalog fallback. TEST-QB-067: requires_explicit_direct_desktop_recovery. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-REFRESHES-WITHOUT-OVERLAPS-OR-CROSS-CONTEXT-RESULTS: Events/reconnect/manual/configured polling refresh data without overlap; discard old-context replies; failures retain only matching-context last-good data with stale/error state. Manual refresh and events coalesce with the active request; reconnect/configuration/workspace/session changes invalidate old generations, including late successful replies after cancellation. Hiding or disposing the view stops display polling; revealing resumes in the current context. Polling bounds and default match QbrainSettings, and failed reads never become empty successes. TEST-QB-026: refreshes_without_overlaps_or_cross_context_results. TDD: P2.

AC-QB-KEEPS-PANEL-REFRESH-INDEPENDENT-OF-AGENT-EXECUTION: Browsing/refresh create no model calls or agent turns; hidden stops needless display polling, not audit/enforcement. TEST-QB-027: keeps_panel_refresh_independent_of_agent_execution. TDD: P2.

AC-QB-RENDERS-SESSION-LOG-AND-TODO-CONTENT-AS-INERT-DATA: Session Log and TODO content is displayed as data. ANSI/OSC/CSI sequences, HTML, scripts, remote resources and instruction-like text in server fields cannot execute code, alter terminal/window/clipboard state, initiate automatic network access, invoke a tool, mutate records or approve an action. Renderers safely represent such content while preserving the canonical value and existing explicit detail/copy security rules. This holds for summary, detail, error, loading-to-loaded updates and restored views in both TUI and desktop. TEST cases: OSC clipboard and hyperlink escapes; CSI cursor controls; HTML/script and remote image content; malformed Unicode; instruction-like text; status/error field injection; narrow live/restored views; explicit safe detail and copy. TEST-QB-074: renders_session_log_and_todo_content_as_inert_data. TDD: P2. Staged regressions: P3, P4.

AC-QB-BOUNDS-INDIVIDUAL-RECORD-AND-DETAIL-PAYLOAD-PROCESSING: A single oversized or malformed record, detail value or streamed response cannot cause unbounded transport buffering or UI work. The slice contract defines supported byte/item limits and recoverable boundary outcomes before implementation. Supported complete data remains available without silent loss; an over-limit or malformed response is explicitly failed/stale with actionable expansion or recovery behavior and is never shown as confirmed complete truncated data. Cancellation/context change releases work and prevents late rendering under another context. Ordinary navigation and governance remain responsive. TEST cases: One huge item in a small page; exact byte limit and one over; many small items; malformed encoding; endless chunk stream; cancellation midway; repeated expansion; old-context completion; full supported data remains available. TEST-QB-076: bounds_individual_record_and_detail_payload_processing. TDD: P2. Staged regressions: P3, P4.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Replacing a turn clears omitted scalars and collections and preserves the workspace stamp on children (existing behavior; SessionLogServiceReplaceDeleteTests.ReplaceTurnAsync_ClearsOmittedScalarsAndCollections, ReplaceTurnAsync_PreservesWorkspaceStampOnChildren).

Replacing a section changes only that section; an empty payload clears it; clearing a section removes all its items; additive upsert never removes items (existing; SessionLogServiceReplaceDeleteTests.ReplaceTurnSectionAsync_ReplacesOnlyNamedSection, ReplaceTurnSectionAsync_EmptyPayload_ClearsSection, ClearTurnSectionAsync_RemovesAllItemsInSection, UpsertTurnAsync_StaysAdditive_DoesNotRemoveExistingItems).

Item delete removes exactly the addressed item (string sections by value, commits by SHA, actions by order) and returns false for an unknown key (existing; SessionLogServiceReplaceDeleteTests.DeleteTurnItemAsync_StringSection_RemovesByValue, DeleteTurnItemAsync_Commit_RemovesBySha, DeleteTurnItemAsync_Action_RemovesByOrder, DeleteTurnItemAsync_UnknownKey_ReturnsFalse).
Replacing an unknown section throws ArgumentException (existing; SessionLogServiceReplaceDeleteTests.ReplaceTurnSectionAsync_UnknownSection_Throws).

Within a turn, dialog, commit and context ordinals stay unique across PATCH batches, each appended item taking an ordinal after the existing ones, also when writes to one turn (a dialog append, a PATCH, a PUT turn replace, a section replace or clear) are committed at the same moment: each such write either applies with ordinals distinct from every other item of that collection or is refused, storing nothing, with an error McpErrorClassifier reports as retryable; deleting a dialog item by its ordinal removes exactly that item; when legacy rows share a key, a delete by that key is refused with an ArgumentException naming how many items match and deletes nothing (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 A7, triage-report-36d2da23; concurrent writes triage-report-905c3ac1b6af4d57b9c24c2383642379, operator decision 2026-10-16 "Fix it in this plan"; SessionLogServiceTests mock gate OrdinalAssertion_AcceptsDistinctOrdinalsAndRejectsARepeatedOrdinal, then UpsertTurnAsync_TwoPatchBatches_KeepDialogCommitAndContextOrdinalsUnique, DeleteTurnItemAsync_DialogOrdinalAfterPatchBatches_RemovesExactlyOneItem, DeleteTurnItemAsync_AmbiguousLegacyKey_RefusesAndDeletesNothing; SessionLogConcurrentTurnWriteTests mock gate ConcurrentTurnWriteOutcomeAssertion_AcceptsDistinctOrRetryableRefusalAndRejectsDuplicateOrPartialWrite, then TurnWrites_InterleavedOnOneTurn_StoreDistinctOrdinalsOrRefuseRetryably and TurnWrites_TwoFirstInsertsOfOneRequestId_LeaveOneTurnRow; SessionLogConcurrentTurnWriteIntegrationTests on temporary instances).

An item whose key contains a slash is deleted through DELETE .../sections/{section}/items with the key in the itemKey query value, which the client sends and the server passes to the service decoded; the path-segment route stays for keys without a slash (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 A8, triage-report-ed3b0381; SessionLogClientRequestBodyTests mock gate ItemKeyUriAssertion_AcceptsQueryKeyAndRejectsPathSegmentKey and DeleteTurnItemAsync_SendsItemKeyInQueryString; SessionLogControllerDeleteItemTests DeleteTurnItemByQueryAsync_KeyWithSlash_DeletesThroughService and DeleteTurnItemRoutes_QueryActionBindsItemKeyFromQueryAndPathActionRemains; SessionLogDeleteItemRoutingTests DeleteByQuery_KeyWithSlashes_DeletesThatItemOnly and UnknownKeyAndEncodedPathSegment_DeleteNothing on a temporary instance).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Opening mcp-web for an authenticated workspace renders fleet, task bank, and header controls on one page.

functional.title: Orchestration cockpit in mcp-web

acceptanceCriteria.text: Dashboard title and path equal the bound workspace name and workspacePath from MCP workspace APIs.
Switching workspace retargets agent pool, TODOs, and session logs to that workspace only.
No .prompter-hawk or other third-party mission directory is required for the dashboard to function.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL treat an MCP workspace as the Prompter Hawk "mission": one named project folder shared by all agents. The operator can bind the dashboard to an existing registered workspace; mcp-web SHALL NOT invent a parallel mission store.
functional.title: Workspace is the mission

acceptanceCriteria.text: Fleet panel lists every configured pooled agent with one of off, idle, working, waiting-for-feedback.
Start and Stop on one agent call AgentPool start/stop and the status updates without a full reload.
Start All and Stop All act on every listed agent and report per-agent success or failure.

Recycle on one agent calls AgentPool recycle, the agent returns to idle or off without requiring a browser reload, and in-flight TODO status is preserved or marked failed according to the pool result.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL show each pooled agent as off, idle, working, or waiting-for-feedback, and SHALL start, stop, recycle, start-all, and stop-all through the agent pool API.
functional.title: Agent fleet lifecycle and status

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every TODO in the bound workspace appears in exactly one lane derived from status and tags.
Creating a TODO from the bank uses the MCP TODO API and never writes docs/todo.yaml or TODO.yaml directly.
Lane filters by agent assignee and priority match the stored TODO fields.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL present MCP TODOs in lanes equivalent to Prompter Hawk task categories: tentative, pending, in progress, blocked, feedback-required, recurring, and completed. MCP TODO storage remains the only source of truth.
functional.title: TODO task bank lanes

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two pending TODOs assigned to two idle agents both enter in_progress without a third operator prompt.
Closing the browser does not cancel in-progress pool work.
Reopening mcp-web shows those TODOs in their live statuses from the store.

functional.body: The operator SHALL be able to create or approve TODOs and leave. Eligible idle agents SHALL pick up pending work in parallel. Returning to mcp-web SHALL show current status without the operator babysitting a chat.
functional.title: Fire-and-forget parallel dispatch

acceptanceCriteria.text: A TODO saved with a daily 06:00 UTC schedule appears in the recurring lane.
When the schedule fires, a pending TODO exists for that template without a manual click.
Disabling the schedule stops further firings and leaves historical TODOs intact.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL let the operator attach a cron-style schedule (hourly, daily, weekly, or custom) to a TODO so MCP recreates or reopens that work on the schedule (daily test+fix, weekly docs, north-star summary).
functional.title: Recurring scheduled TODOs

acceptanceCriteria.text: Workspace context is present in every dispatched run in that workspace.
Agent persona/prompt overrides workspace text for that agent only.
TODO description is the most specific layer and is included in the run payload.

functional.body: Context configured at workspace, then agent, then TODO SHALL merge in that order and travel automatically into the dispatched agent run so the operator does not paste the same instructions into every task.
functional.title: Hierarchical context inheritance

acceptanceCriteria.text: Retry on a failed TODO enqueues new work bound to the same TODO id or a recorded retry child linked to it.
The retry payload includes the original description plus workspace and agent context.
The UI does not require the operator to locate a prior chat transcript to retry.

functional.body: A failed or completed TODO SHALL be retryable from mcp-web in one action that reuses the original TODO identity, hierarchical context, and prior session linkage. The operator SHALL NOT copy-paste prompts.
functional.title: One-click retry with preserved context

acceptanceCriteria.text: Selecting a working agent streams new dialog and tool_call items without a manual refresh.
A completed TODO still opens its full message history.
Live peek reads session log APIs; it does not scrape terminal windows.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL show live reasoning, tool calls, model id, and message history for a selected in-progress agent or TODO from the MCP session log and event stream (Prompter Hawk Live Peek).
functional.title: Live peek of agent work

acceptanceCriteria.text: A 24-hour burn chart renders from session-log token counts.
Burn rate above the workspace baseline uses a distinct warning color; at or below baseline uses a distinct normal color.
Progress metrics include commits, net line change, peak concurrent working agents, and completions for the current UTC day.
Progress metrics show lines added and lines removed as separate counts, not only net change.
Progress metrics include files analyzed for the current UTC day.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL chart token burn versus a workspace baseline (color-coded) and show today's lines added/removed, commits, files analyzed, peak parallelism, and TODO completions.
functional.title: Token burn and daily progress

acceptanceCriteria.text: A feedback-required TODO appears in the feedback lane while other in_progress TODOs stay in progress.
Submitting feedback resumes or fails that TODO through MCP APIs.
The request records what to test, an optional command, a question, and response options.

functional.body: When an agent needs validation, mcp-web SHALL queue a non-blocking feedback request. Other agents SHALL continue. The operator answers on their schedule with structured options plus free text.
functional.title: Human feedback queue

acceptanceCriteria.text: With orchestrator enabled, an idle agent with an empty pending queue results in at least one tentative TODO.
Tentative TODOs are not assigned to running agents until the operator approves.
Disabling orchestrator stops new proposals; existing tentative items remain until dismissed or approved.

functional.body: An optional orchestrator mode SHALL detect idle agents and create tentative TODOs for operator approval. Tentative items SHALL NOT dispatch until approved (Prompter Hawk Team Captain, mapped to MCP TODOs).
functional.title: Idle orchestrator proposes tentative TODOs

acceptanceCriteria.text: Saving an allow src/* and deny .env rule persists through the workspace policy API.
A denied path or tool is rejected with a visible error on the agent run, not silently ignored.
Rules are visible and editable in mcp-web without editing YAML by hand.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL let the operator set per-agent or workspace allow/deny rules for tools (including shell, read, write, edit) and path globs (for example allow src/*, deny .env). Denied actions fail closed.
functional.title: Tool and path allow/deny UI

acceptanceCriteria.text: Two agents in one workspace can show two different providers and models.
Changing an agent model persists and is used on the next start.
mcp-web does not add a billed proxy; it uses operator-configured provider credentials already known to QBrain.AI.

functional.body: Each pooled agent SHALL be assignable in mcp-web to a configured backend (Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, Grok, or other already-supported MCP providers) and model id, mixing providers in one workspace.
functional.title: Per-agent multi-provider backends

acceptanceCriteria.text: A completed TODO with a session-log commit action displays the SHA on the card.
Disabling the mapping hides SHAs but does not delete session-log actions.

functional.body: When task-to-commit mapping is enabled, completing a TODO SHALL show linked commit SHAs from session-log commit actions on that TODO's card.
functional.title: TODO to git commit linkage

acceptanceCriteria.text: Default mcp-web configuration has no third-party analytics endpoint for prompt or file payloads.
Automated tests fail if a dashboard bundle sends prompt text or file bodies to a non-MCP, non-provider host.
Operator secrets are not rendered in live peek beyond existing session-log redaction rules.

functional.body: mcp-web SHALL NOT upload prompts, file contents, or diffs to a product analytics host. Code leaves the machine only toward AI providers the operator already configured on QBrain.AI.
functional.title: mcp-web local-first privacy

acceptanceCriteria.text: At 1280x800, fleet and task bank are both visible without horizontal clipping of primary controls.

functional.title: Desktop and mobile viewports

acceptanceCriteria.text: A TODO with an incomplete prerequisite appears in the blocked lane and is not auto-dispatched.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Editing an agent prompt and restarting that agent still uses the new prompt.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Saving hourly and daily caps persists on the agent configuration.

Architecture audit and remediation across `QBrainAi.Support.Mcp` SHALL enforce:
- Stateful services, registries, managers, and providers must be DI-owned (`singleton` or `scoped`) and must not be instantiated via `new` or `ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance` outside composition-root registration paths.
- Authoritative mutable state must have a single owner in DI; peer services must pull current state from that owner instead of receiving pushed state payloads.
- Observable state contracts must expose change signaling via `INotifyPropertyChanged` for data-availability/change notification, without embedding mutable payload transfer in event arguments.
- Race-condition remediation must prioritize ownership/lifetime design in DI (single owner + pull model); fire-and-forget propagation and ad-hoc synchronization used as state-sharing mechanisms are prohibited.
- Automated validation must cover DI registration lifetimes and notification semantics for remediated services.

technical.body: Project history excludes secrets and automatic operational audit. This does NOT make audit local-only: every host retains permanent local audit and an append-only outbox delivers sanitized records to the hub unversioned ledger independently of project commits. AuditRecord key=(OriginNodeId,RecordId UUID); fields ProjectId,EntityKind,EntityId,OriginSequence int64,OccurredUtc,Actor,Action,PayloadVersion,PayloadHash,Payload. POST audit/batches validates token/project, inserts atomically by key and returns per-record durable receipts. Same key/hash is already_received; same key/different hash=409 audit_id_conflict. No UPDATE/DELETE permission. Local pruning is forbidden. Migration backfills TODO and generic audit history with counts/hashes and receipts. Credential values are excluded at capture, not silently replicated.

technical.body:
Concurrent sessionlog_delete_turn operations on a single session SHALL be serialized through a process-wide per-session gate so a burst (observed: 13 parallel deletes) cannot exhaust or poison the SQL Server connection pool; deletes on different sessions SHALL still run concurrently; the deployed SqlClient ConnectRetryCount=6/ConnectRetryInterval=10s defaults SHALL be preserved. Acceptance Criteria: (AC1) acquiring the per-session lock for the same key blocks a second acquirer until release, while a different key acquires without blocking (KeyedAsyncLock); (AC2) DeleteTurnAsync continues to soft-delete a turn and refresh the parent turn count correctly under the lock. Origin: BUG-TRIAGE-079 (concurrent gated deletes poisoned the pool with SqlClient error 19 then 40 for ~3 minutes while SQL Server stayed up). Note: pool poisoning is a SQL-Server-runtime property not unit-reproducible; the deterministic serialization proof is the KeyedAsyncLock unit test, with SessionLogService.DeleteTurnAsync wrapped in the per-session lock keyed by sourceType/sessionId. Validated by TEST-MCP-DB-006.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-105; TEST: TEST-MCP-138, TEST-MCP-139, TEST-MCP-140, TEST-MCP-DB-006

acceptanceCriteria.text: For SQLite, PostgreSQL and SQL Server, the model configured the way startup configures it has no pending changes against that provider's migrations, so every DateTimeOffset column the migrations create matches the converted model (ProviderMigrationModelTests.ProviderMigrations_HaveNoPendingModelChanges).

On SQL Server, RequirementsRecoveryRuns.DeletedAtUtc is datetime2 and a soft-deleted recovery run reads back its DeletedAtUtc as the same UTC instant (TEST-MCP-102, SqlServer_RequirementsRecoveryRun_SoftDelete_RoundTripsUtcDeletedAt).

technical.body: McpDbContext stores every DateTimeOffset property as a UTC DateTime through DateTimeOffsetToUtcDateTimeConverter, applied to all DateTimeOffset properties in ConfigureConventions, so the SQLite provider can translate timestamp predicates and ordering to SQL; every timestamp in the schema is UTC, so the conversion is lossless. Each provider's migrations create the columns the converted model maps; on SQL Server that is datetime2 (RequirementsRecoveryRuns.DeletedAtUtc was created as datetimeoffset and corrected by AddHostileReviewTables, PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B8).
technical.notes: Recorded 2026-10-15 from the rule DateTimeOffsetToUtcDateTimeConverter.cs and McpDbContext.ConfigureConventions already state and cite; the store never held the record (operator decision 2026-10-15 "Approve all three (Recommended)", PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B8).

technical.body:
All plugins call typed server/client/MCP/REPL contracts; no raw SQL/CLI fallback. Status DTO includes projectId, branch, localHead, publishedHead, observedUtc, dirty, ahead, behind, publicationState, incomingTarget, connectivity, reviewCount, oldestReviewAgeSeconds, waitingLocalWorkAgeSeconds, auditPendingCount, hubEpoch, workerEpoch. Capability contract version1 is negotiated; unknown version=409 unsupported_contract. Administrative maintenance.preflight/attest/status and migration commands share the same typed service as Nuke. Stable error envelope={code, message, requestId, projectId, branch, retryable, details}; status codes are locked in the technical contract appendix.

Technical contract appendix (TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010): all below routes are under /qbrainai/federation unless the commits route specifies the project/branch path. Every mutation requires requestId UUID and authenticated subject; node network requests additionally carry the project-scoped reference token. Responses carry contractVersion=1 and the stable error envelope. Path/body ProjectId mismatch is403 unauthorized_project. No endpoint accepts credentials in URL, argv or persisted receipts.

Read/status routes: GET capabilities returns200 {contractVersion,capabilities}; GET projects/{projectId}/status returns200 the status DTO; GET projects/{projectId}/branches returns200 {items:[{name,head,dirty,publishedHead}]}; GET conflicts and GET conflicts/{reviewId} return200 review records filtered by membership. POST control/poll returns200 {hubEpoch,subscriptions}; reads never acknowledge work. POST control/report validates observed generation and worker epoch, returns200 the durable receipt or409 the named fence error. Poll/report use control scope; reads use read scope.

Mutation routes: POST enroll returns201 the enrollment (or200 the same idempotent enrollment); POST projects/{projectId}/branches creates201 {branch,head}; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/select returns200 {sessionId,branch,head} after local lease validation; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits returns201 {commitHash,publicationState}, or200 the same commit on retry. POST publication/accept returns200 {requestId,hubEpoch,publishedHead,publishedGeneration,receiptId} only after the guarded ref update is durable. POST branches/merge and POST conflicts/{reviewId}/resolve bind expected heads and return201 the new commit; a conflict returns202 {outcome:needs_review,reviewId} while the live head stays unchanged. Share/merge/publication require publish scope plus branch permission. Enrollment requires enroll scope and the operator owner-binding approval.

POST audit/batches accepts {requestId,projectId,records:[AuditRecord]}, returns200 {receipts:[{originNodeId,recordId,payloadHash,outcome,receivedUtc}]}, and requires audit scope. Every record must match the token/project and batch ProjectId. Any invalid record rejects the whole batch before insert. Exact duplicate is already_received; payload mismatch is409 audit_id_conflict. POST ids/reservations accepts {requestId,projectId,entityKind,humanId,nodeId}, requires publish scope and returns201 the reservation or200 its exact retry; another owner gets409 human_id_reserved. POST maintenance/preflight and POST maintenance/attest, GET maintenance/status and POST migration/{plan|dry-run|run|resume|verify|export-project|export-todos|cutover|abort}, GET migration/status are operator-only local service operations. They are exposed through typed clients and Nuke, never public node-admin capabilities. A long migration returns202 {migrationId,status}; status/verify return200 a receipt, and a denied readiness check never performs cutover.

Stable failure mapping:401 invalid_token;403 unauthorized_project;409 head_changed, working_set_changed, lease_lost, branch_busy, stale_review, stale_worker_epoch, hub_epoch_changed, ambiguous_legacy_id, human_id_reserved, human_id_unreserved, target_not_empty, maintenance_not_ready, migration_source_changed, migration_verification_failed, incompatible_schema, unsupported_contract and publication_required;422 secret_detected, dependency_cycle and unsupported_provider;501 unsupported_capability;503 identity_unavailable or remote_unavailable. TLS rejection produces the local transport code tls_peer_untrusted with no HTTP response and no request sent. Missing required fields return400 invalid_request. Missing authorized resources return404 not_found; project authorization precedes existence disclosure. Malformed/unsupported token is401; valid token lacking project rights is403.

Outcome fields are not HTTP errors: committed_locally, already_received, waiting_local_work and needs_review remain visible through200 status/report responses. A requested live mutation blocked by drafts returns409 waiting_local_work; an integration that durably creates review returns202 needs_review. dependency_cycle is a validationErrors entry on that review as well as422 for a directly invalid local mutation. retryable=true is restricted to transient503/transport failures; all stale-head/fence/review errors require reread and a fresh validated action. Idempotent retries with the same requestId but different payload return409 request_id_conflict. No automatic retry creates a different commit.

Test fixtures capture actual content hashes as symbols C0,A1,B1,H1,M1,M2,S1 rather than hardcoding unstable engine hashes. Each symbol is immutable within the run manifest. Given/When/Then compares exact hash equality, specified parent sets, row values, status codes and error codes against that manifest; a successful result must never be inferred solely from an empty queue. Capture UTC timestamps and a fake clock for exact15-minute/24-hour age boundaries. All plan phase IDs use Ph0-Ph8; priority values remain separate.

Plugin completeness is checked by PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics, PluginRecoveryControls, PluginIdentityDiagnostics, PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial, PluginEffectBoundary and PluginEditingOwnership in their mapped contracts. Ph7 owns their plugin bindings; earlier phases own server behavior. Standalone and explicit DirectProxy compatibility remain under FR-MCP-077/TR-MCP-FED-001; this does not reinstate versioned LocalProxy forwarding.

Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-096. GET /health is liveness-only (tags live: self plus FederationUpstreamHealthCheck) with no storage connectivity check, so when the database backend is unreachable the server still answers Healthy and echoes the trust nonce correctly while every persistence call fails. Observed live on 2026-07-20 when the SQL host was powered off: marker trust passed, then todo_list returned a raw SqlClient "Named Pipes Provider, error: 40" string, sessionlog_query returned a misleading "transient failure, consider EnableRetryOnFailure" hint, triage_report returned a bare "an error occurred", and the plugin wrapper returned an opaque 30-second timeout, so no caller could tell that storage was simply down. The server SHALL expose storage reachability on the health path, either by degrading the status or by an explicit storage field, WITHOUT breaking the nonce echo that marker trust bootstrap depends on. Backend-unavailable conditions SHALL surface as one typed error consistently across REST and the MCP tools, distinguishable from a malformed request. Coverage SHALL simulate an unreachable store and assert the misleading Healthy result before the fix.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-143; TEST: TEST-MCP-194, TEST-MCP-REPL-040

technical.body: **Exception Logging in Catch Blocks** *(DIRECTIVE)* - Every `catch` block that handles an exception must log the exception. Unexpected exceptions must use `LogError` with `ex.ToString()` as the message body. Expected/anticipated exceptions (e.g., `OperationCanceledException` on shutdown, `InvalidOperationException` for process-already-exited races, validation exceptions returned as HTTP 4xx) must use `LogWarning` with `ex.ToString()`. Catch blocks must not silently swallow exceptions with empty bodies or comments-only. The only permitted exception is re-throwing (`throw;`) without logging, where the exception will be logged by an outer handler.

`TodoValidator` SHALL validate persisted TODO IDs against the canonical regex set `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)+-\d{3}$` or `^ISSUE-\d+$` for create/update dependency paths across all configured TODO storage providers (`yaml` and `database` per TR-MCP-TODO-005). `ISSUE-NEW` SHALL remain a create-time alias handled before persistence, not a persisted TODO identifier. `SessionLogIdentifierValidator` SHALL validate session/request IDs using canonical timestamped patterns and enforce exact source-type prefix parity (`SessionId` starts with `{sourceType}-` or `{agent}-`). Invalid values return HTTP 400 at controller boundaries and `ArgumentException` for direct service invocation.

**Covered by:** `TodoValidator`, `TodoService`, `EfTodoService`, `TodoCreationService`, `SessionLogIdentifierValidator`, `SessionLogController`, `SessionLogService`

`ParseableEventFormatter` SHALL emit no more than 250 top-level fields for any individual Parseable event payload. The formatter SHALL always preserve the canonical Parseable metadata keys (`timestamp`, `level`, `message`, and `exception` when present), SHALL prevent user-supplied structured properties from overwriting those reserved keys, and SHALL drop excess non-reserved properties once the remaining field budget is exhausted. Property selection for retained non-reserved fields SHALL be deterministic so tests and operational analysis can reason about which fields survive truncation.

Each official plugin's UserPromptSubmit hook entry (the hooks/scripts/user-prompt-submit.ps1 that plugins/core/hooks-templates/generate-wrappers.ps1 writes, lib/user-prompt-submit.ps1 for Codex) adds the plugin's required-memory block from its memory-context.ps1 (the descriptor's prefix and the effective memories, or the explicit empty fallback when there are none or the fetch fails) to the hook output's additionalContext whatever the turn-open status, and keeps the hook's other output fields and its exit code; a plugin without the helper gets the hook output unchanged; the memory fetch keeps to the hook's deadline (TR-MCP-REPL-012 AC-001): with less than one second left it is not started and the empty fallback is rendered, and otherwise its timeout is no longer than the whole seconds left (triage-report-f01b3544; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 F2; proved by the plugin core's user-prompt memory-injection Pester suite, a mock gate and four bindings, which cite this criterion; and each plugin's tests/MemoryInjection.Tests.ps1 user-prompt-submit cases).

technical.body: Every child process that the build's infrastructure test suite starts with redirected standard output and standard error SHALL run through one shared helper that bounds the wait for the child to exit, bounds the wait for its redirected output to close after it exits, drains both streams concurrently, kills the child's process tree when the exit timeout expires or the caller cancels, and starts dotnet children with --disable-build-servers, so that no child, descendant, or persistent build server can stall the suite.
technical.notes: Implementation detail of FR-MCP-BUILD-001 "Tooling for repeatable builds" (operator, 2026-10-10: "Now, the TR are implementation detail of the FR."); the build's infrastructure test suite is build infrastructure (operator, 2026-10-10: "Build.Tests is infrastructure, not application and should not be treated as unit tests."). Introduced for BUG-BUILD-007 (triage-report-c381e4c99d284e0dbc1ec443c221ca59). Root cause observed live on 2026-10-10 at 22:14Z (Linux, SDK 10.0.201) during the BUG-BUILD-006 trim-inventory run: the infrastructure test process (PID 2575389, 0 s CPU over 850 s, no child processes) was blocked on EOF of a dotnet child that had already exited; the other ends of both redirected pipes (pipe:[16191191] stdout, pipe:[16191192] stderr) were held as fd 1 and fd 2 by an MSBuild worker node (MSBuild.dll /nodemode:1 /nodeReuse:true, PID 2575659) that the child's build had spawned and that had been reparented to the user systemd (PPID 1082); the node also held the test process's stdin. Node reuse keeps such a node alive after the build, so EOF never arrives; when an idle reusable node already exists the build connects to it instead and nothing inherits the pipes, which explains the earlier passing run. The trim-analysis warning inventory tests bound only WaitForExitAsync (20 minutes); the await of their output tasks that follows is unbounded. Receipt: bug-build-007-evidence.log.txt. Refined 2026-10-10 after HV round 1 (finding F-B7) by three bounded experiments; receipts in docs/receipts/_bug-build-003-009-20261010T224959Z/ (bug-build-007-evidence-note.md and bug-build-007-experiment1..3.log.txt). The live log's elapsed times were read about five minutes apart, so they do not show the node predating the test. Provenance: in every experiment the node's parent PID, read while the build child ran, was the child. Mechanism: dotnet test sets MSBUILDENSURESTDOUTFORTASKPROCESSES=1 for vstest.console, the test host, and the test executable (the dotnet test process itself has it unset), so every build an infrastructure test case starts inherits it. With it set, MSBuild starts worker nodes without redirecting their standard streams, and a node spawned by the build inherits the build's redirected stdout and stderr (the output stayed open 30 s after exit). Without it, as from a plain shell, the node gets its own streams and the output closes at once. Node reuse keeps the node alive after the build. When an idle node with a matching handshake exists, the build reuses it and spawns nothing, so the hang is intermittent. With --disable-build-servers the node exits with the build and the output closes at once, even with the variable set.
technical.title: Build infrastructure tests bound every child process and its redirected output

acceptanceCriteria.text: On a Windows host the target runs Category=Integration cases except those tagged Platform=Linux; on a Linux host it runs them except those tagged Platform=Windows; untagged integration cases run on both.

MigrationIntegrationTests runs the Category=Integration cases of every integration-owned test project the build declares, each project with its own TRX under the run's --test-run-id, except the cases the build declares held out: from the server integration test project only the Category=Integration cases of two classes, the requirement-scope REPL integration tests and the QuadBrain Ollama endpoint integration tests, selected by class name, run (operator 2026-10-29: "Run the 2 classes, AC first (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R8B-F2), and the ACID and transaction-security integration test projects are not run by the lane until PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 merges and their failing cases are resolved (TODO IMPL-TXNINTEGRATION-001). The lane runs no unit-owned or infrastructure-owned test project, and no validation, AI review or plugin integration project, which has its own target (operator 2026-11-06: "Separate projects + AC (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R14-F4). Every case tagged Platform=Linux or Platform=Windows runs and passes in the lane of a host of that platform, and a lane project whose filter selects no case fails the lane instead of passing empty (operator 2026-10-29: "Lane ACs (Recommended)"; holistic review findings PLAN-1 and BLD-1).

The run log names the selection filter (filter text only). The host filter, each lane project's filter and each lane project's TRX name are outputs of one lane composition that the target uses and logs as given, proved by the build's infrastructure test cases over that composition (operator 2026-10-29: "Lane ACs (Recommended)"; holistic review finding BLD-3; operator 2026-10-30: "F1: AC-3 wording (Recommended)").

Every integration case MigrationIntegrationTests runs that needs a QBrain.AI instance uses a temporary instance it owns, whether a server process on a free port, an in-process host or a stdio host, with a test-owned workspace, marker and database, never the live server, its marker or its API key. A case that needs a server asserts on that instance's answers and fails when it cannot reach it; it never catches the failure and passes. A database selection outside the owned root is refused before the instance reads or writes that database. The rules for the instance's environment, database selection and consumers are FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 ac-4 (operator 2026-10-29: "Strengthen ACs, fix both (Recommended)", "Run the 2 classes, AC first (Recommended)" and "Lane ACs (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-30: "FR-MCP-TESTRESOURCE-001 (Recommended)"; hostile validation findings R8B-F2 and R8B-F3; holistic review findings PLAN-6, PLAN-7, RINT-1, RINT-2 and RINT-3).

Test-project ownership: given a declared project role (unit, integration or infrastructure) and a supplied case inventory, the unit test selection accepts only unit-owned projects whose cases are all unit cases, the integration test selection accepts only integration-owned projects whose cases are all integration cases, infrastructure-owned projects are accepted by neither selection, and every valid selection preserves every intended case exactly once (none omitted, none duplicated). A unit-owned project holding an integration case, or an integration-owned project holding a unit case, is rejected. (Hostile validation round 14, finding R14-F4, the reviewer's proposed criterion test-project-ownership with a third role for infrastructure-owned projects; added under the operator's 2026-11-06 choice "Separate projects + AC (Recommended)" and MEMORY-BESTPRACTICE-001 rules 4.1 and 4.4.) The build derives each selected project's case inventory from that project's own discovered cases at run time, never from a recorded count, and Test and MigrationIntegrationTests fail before reporting success when a unit-owned project holds a Category=Integration case or an integration-owned project holds a case without it. A test that cites this criterion or AC-8 judges ownership over a runtime-discovered inventory, or over a scripted inventory stated as synthetic. No test asserts a recorded per-project or total case count as the current layout. Runtime discovery fails the target before any test runs when the all-case result is empty, any result repeats an identity, a filtered result holds an identity the all-case result lacks, or the runner output lacks the test-list header. Parsing accepts only indented case identities after the header and ends the case list at the first unindented line.

Quarantined test cases (operator 2026-11-07: "Find the AC matching the test behavior.  If none match, quarantine them (keep, but descope them) for later manual investigation."): a test case whose behavior matches no acceptance criterion in the requirement store is kept, never deleted, skipped or weakened, and carries the trait Quarantine=NoMatchingCriterion. Test and MigrationIntegrationTests run no quarantined case, and the selection filter each logs shows the exclusion; TestGroups still runs a quarantined case when its class is named; the build's test-project ownership counts quarantined cases per project apart from the unit and integration cases, and each selection still runs every case that is not quarantined exactly once.

Every class a group names runs at least one case in its project's TRX; a named class that runs no case fails the target and the failure names that class (operator 2026-11-02: "Add both ACs (Recommended)"). A class counts as run only when an executed result's test, joined to its definition by test id, belongs to that class (its definition's class name is the class, as the whole name or its last segment). A definition with no executed result, a namespace segment, and a display name or argument that mentions the class do not count; a custom display name counts through its test's class (operator 2026-11-02: "Strengthen 5 ACs, fix all 8 (Recommended)"; hostile validation finding R9-F1).

acceptanceCriteria.text: Reuse P1.4 Windows lexical normalization, preserve case, and reject distinct old keys converging before any database mutation.
Apply requires successful verified backup; all database changes and FK validation occur in one transaction; repeat apply is a no-op.
Dry-run inventory and planning run only on a database copy; report mappings, table and workspace counts, and retained manual triage hashes without secrets.
HTTP and STDIO startup refuse legacy Windows workspace ids and point to --workspace-path-rekey.
Recompute only derivable triage, handoff, and federation identities; repoint children; preserve manual triage hashes and rewrite token-store keys with file backup.

technical.body: WorkspaceIdentityPath.NormalizeLexicalPath emits '/' for Windows paths (UNC keeps leading '//'; \\?\ device prefixes stripped to drive or // form); BuildStorageKey becomes windows:C:/WORKSPACES/EXAMPLE style. IsRemoteWindowsPath, IsNormalizedPathWithinRoot and NormalizeLocalAdministrativeShareAlias accept both separators. A ToNativePath helper produces backslash paths only for Win32 CreateFile/GetFinalPathNameByHandle, \\?\ long-path prefixes and cmd.exe arguments. Persisted data is rewritten by an explicit maintenance command --workspace-path-rekey (decision D5, 2026-10-07) modelled on McpDatabaseEncryptionTransitionCommand: required backup unless --dry-run, report with old->new mapping and before/after counts; one transaction per database with foreign keys deferred or suspended and fully re-validated (decision D6: SQLite defer_foreign_keys, SQL Server NOCHECK then WITH CHECK CHECK, PostgreSQL DEFERRABLE + SET CONSTRAINTS ALL DEFERRED); set-based UPDATE per workspace column from a mapping table limited to Windows-shaped values; C# recomputation of hashed values (federation GlobalWorkspaceId/CanonicalWorkspaceId and hub hash-keyed Workspaces rows, TriageGroups GroupKey/GroupId with repointed children, HandoffIngestionRuns ReplayIdentity); FileGitHubWorkspaceTokenStore keys rewritten. No legacy dual-key lookup (decision D7): a startup guard refuses to start while any Windows-shaped workspace id still contains a backslash. Enrolled proxies are re-enrolled once after deploy (the Windows proxy in the original deployment). Plan: docs/plans/2026-10-07-federation-fixes.md section 4c.
technical.notes: P1.5 operator decisions 2026-10-16: Policy A uses existing Windows lexical normalizer including device-prefix stripping and case preservation. Distinct old keys converging abort before mutation. Manual triage keys are SHA-256(workspacePath|manual|random GUID); retain their GroupKey/GroupId because GUID is not stored. Only recompute derived identities verified from persisted inputs. Worktree-only implementation and disposable fixture/copy tests; no live apply, service operations, deploy, or merge. Current task explicitly requests requirements/tests first (red), then implementation.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A UserPromptSubmit prompt made only of host events, Claude Code task notifications (<task-notification>...</task-notification>) and subagent hand-backs (<agent-message ...>...</agent-message>), is not an operator request: the hook opens no session-log turn, supersedes nothing, leaves current-turn.yaml unchanged and reports status system-event; a prompt with any other text, including an operator message after such a block, opens its turn as before (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D4, triage-report-5c7278cd; HostEventAssertion_AcceptsEventsOnlyAndRejectsRequestText, HostEvent_Classifier_PinnedShapes, HookEventAssertion_AcceptsNoTurnAndRejectsOpenOrSupersede, UserPromptSubmit_HostEvent_OpensNoTurnAndKeepsCurrentTurn, UserPromptSubmit_RequestAfterEvent_OpensTurn).

The Claude plugin's hook validator (skills/claude-hook-validation/scripts/validate-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1) and hook installer (skills/claude-hook-wiring/scripts/install-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1) recognize the plugin as enabled from the enabledPlugins object Claude Code writes to settings.json, a key "<plugin name>@<marketplace>" whose value is true, the plugin name being the one in .claude-plugin/plugin.json, whether or not CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is set; from enabledPlugins, a false value, another plugin's key (including one whose name only contains this plugin's name) or no entry is not recognized, the list form stays accepted, and the existing CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT fallback is unchanged. With the plugin enabled and its hooks.json registering the UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PostToolUse hooks, the validator reports valid and the installer adds no settings-level bridge hook, so a repair cannot create a second delivery of the prompt (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D5, triage-report-bd1f4386; EnabledPluginAssertion_AcceptsObjectFormAndRejectsCastOrBooleanBlindRules, EnabledPlugin_BothScripts_PinnedSettingsShapes, Validator_ObjectFormWithoutPluginRoot_ReportsValid, Validator_DisabledObjectForm_ReportsMissing, Installer_ObjectFormWithoutPluginRoot_AddsNoBridgeHooks).

A UserPromptSubmit prompt the hook classifies as a background or hostile-agent brief (MCP_SUBAGENT_ID or GROK_SUBAGENT_ID set, a payload subagent field, or a brief marker), from a host whose identity (MCP_SUBAGENT_ID, else GROK_SUBAGENT_ID, else the hook payload's session_id) differs from the agentSessionId that session-state.yaml records for the root, opens and logs its own session-log turn in the root's session: its local turn state lives in a cache folder of its own keyed by that identity; its first write carries the root's session id and the id of the turn the root's current-turn.yaml names, open or completed, in contextList and the tag background-agent; the root's current-turn.yaml and the root's turn are unchanged, so the session holds both turns in progress. That host's Stop completes its own in-progress turn, with or without recorded work, and never the root's; with MCP_SUBAGENT_ID or GROK_SUBAGENT_ID set, the session-log verbs the agent calls itself reach its own turn. No prompt reuses another prompt's turn or is skipped; a brief whose identity equals the root's, or that has none, is the root host's own prompt and opens a root turn as an operator prompt does. Assumes the root's session-state.yaml is intact; a SessionStart that replaces it is triage-report-a4f43e4c, outside this criterion by operator decision 2026-10-15 (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D3, triage-report-061f30e9; BackgroundTurnAssertion_AcceptsOwnTurnAndRejectsReuseSkipOrSupersede, ScopeIdentityRule_ReferencePassesAndRejectsWrongRules, StopOutcomeAssertion_AcceptsOwnCompletionAndRejectsRootCompletion, ScopeIdentityRule_ShippedFunction_PinnedIdentities, UserPromptSubmit_BackgroundBrief_OpensOwnTurnInRootSession, UserPromptSubmit_BackgroundBrief_CompletedRoot_OpensOwnTurn, UserPromptSubmit_BriefWithRootIdentity_OpensRootTurn, Stop_BackgroundHost_CompletesOwnTurnOnly, SessionLogVerb_SubagentEnvironment_ReachesOwnTurn).

technical.body:
Implements FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002. OllamaServerController lives in the shared test-support sources with no xunit dependency; its probe delegate, executable resolver, process launcher, poll interval, timeout, delay, and clock are injected so the policy is unit-testable without a real Ollama binary. It is linked into the server's unit and integration test projects through the tests' shared build targets following the Validation.Shared linked-source idiom. EnsureRunningAsync probes first, launches only when the probe fails, then polls until the probe succeeds or the timeout elapses; on timeout it terminates any process it started before throwing. A resolver returning no executable throws an InvalidOperationException naming the InstallOllama Nuke target without attempting a launch. StopAsync terminates only a controller-started process and is idempotent. OllamaServerFixture implements IAsyncLifetime over the controller with a real HttpClient probe on /api/tags, a resolver covering PATH, LocalAppData/Programs/Ollama, and the Nuke test-tools ollama directory (ollama.exe on Windows; bin/ollama, the Linux portable layout InstallOllama provisions, on Linux; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 B13), and a launcher running 'ollama serve' that kills the whole process tree; the QuadBrain Ollama endpoint integration tests consume it through IClassFixture. IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-20. Evidence: red gate was a compile failure (CS0234/CS0246, controller type absent); green gate: the Ollama server controller tests 6/0/0 and the server unit suite 1692/0/0. Live proof on PAYTON-LEGION2 with no Ollama running and none on PATH: the QuadBrain Ollama endpoint integration tests went from 3 failed to 4 passed in 3m35s using the portable binary at LocalAppData/McpServer/test-tools/ollama, and after the run zero ollama processes remained with port 11434 not listening.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002; TEST: TEST-MCP-QBOLLAMA-002

acceptanceCriteria.text: The plugin REPL bridge (plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 run with -Method, the REPL surface every agent plugin calls) answers a call that fails before any response envelope arrives (marker refresh failure, REPL executable not found, a timeout, or the REPL exiting without output) with one YAML envelope on stdout of type error whose payload carries code, message (the failure text, or the REPL's exit code when it wrote nothing) and retryable, the code and retryable taken from the plugin's error classification (TR-MCP-TRIAGEERR-001), and the script exits 1; a call that succeeds without output writes nothing; the bridge never writes a bare True or False to stdout (triage-report-eb56d4eb; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 F1; proved by the plugin core's REPL bridge error-envelope Pester suite, a mock gate and three bindings, which cite this criterion).

technical.body:
The REPL host SHALL parse incoming STDIO lines as YAML-formatted command envelopes containing `type`, `payload` with method-specific parameters, and optional `correlationId`/`requestId`. Response envelopes SHALL contain `type` (`result`/`error`/`event`), `payload` with result data or error details, and echoed identifiers. Malformed YAML SHALL emit structured error responses rather than crashing the process.

**Covered by:** `McpServer.Repl.Core` (`IYamlEnvelope`, `IYamlSerializer`, `IReplProtocol`)
technical.title: YAML Envelope Protocol

technical.body:
The REPL host SHALL use DI composition for workflow and service registration. The command loop SHALL inject scoped service instances per command invocation and SHALL NOT instantiate services via `new` or `ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance` outside DI registration paths. Workflows SHALL be registered as scoped services and resolved from the service provider.

**Covered by:** `McpServer.Repl.Host` (`ServiceCollectionExtensions`, `Program.cs`), `McpServer.Repl.Core` workflow interfaces
technical.title: DI-Integrated REPL Host

technical.body:
The REPL host SHALL support graceful startup with command loop initialization, interactive STDIO processing, structured error handling with typed error codes, and clean shutdown on EOF or explicit exit. The command loop SHALL read YAML envelopes from stdin, dispatch to workflow handlers, serialize responses as YAML to stdout, and maintain session context across commands. Unhandled exceptions SHALL emit structured error responses and continue the loop.

**Covered by:** `McpServer.Repl.Host` (`Program.cs`, `AgentStdioHandler`, `InteractiveHandler`), `McpServer.Repl.Core` (`SessionLogErrorEnvelope`)
technical.title: Command Loop Lifecycle

technical.body:
Workflow handlers SHALL implement typed interfaces (`ITodoWorkflow`, `ISessionLogWorkflow`, `IRequirementsWorkflow`, `IGenericClientPassthrough`) with async operation methods. Command dispatch SHALL resolve workflow instances from DI per invocation and SHALL pass deserialized parameters as strongly typed method arguments via YamlDotNet model binding. Command routing SHALL map YAML method names to workflow operations.

**Covered by:** `McpServer.Repl.Core` (`ITodoWorkflow`, `ISessionLogWorkflow`, `IRequirementsWorkflow`, `IGenericClientPassthrough`), `McpServer.Repl.Host` (`TodoWorkflow`, `SessionLogWorkflow`, `RequirementsWorkflow`, `GenericClientPassthrough`)
technical.title: Command Registry and Dispatcher

technical.body:
Command names SHALL use dot-delimited namespaces: `workflow.todo.*`, `workflow.session.*`, `workflow.requirements.*`, `client.*`. Handler implementations SHALL delegate to existing client contracts (`TodoClient`, `SessionLogClient`, `RequirementsClient`, `ContextClient`, `RepoClient`, `DesktopClient`) without duplicating business logic. Workflows SHALL maintain stateful context (TODO selection, session state) within the REPL process.

**Covered by:** `McpServer.Repl.Core` (`TodoCommandShapes`, `SessionLogCommandShapes`, `RequirementsCommandShapes`, `ClientCommandShapes`), `McpServer.Repl.Host` (`TodoWorkflow`, `SessionLogWorkflow`, `RequirementsWorkflow`, `GenericClientPassthrough`)
technical.title: Namespace Organization and Handler Parity

technical.body:
The REPL host SHALL implement marker-file trust bootstrap with signature verification and health nonce challenge before accepting operational commands. API key authentication SHALL use per-workspace token semantics from marker files. The host SHALL detect API key rotation between commands via marker file watch and SHALL emit warnings when tokens become stale. Trust verification SHALL use the same contract as PowerShell modules.

**Covered by:** `McpServer.Repl.Core` (`ITrustBootstrapService`, `IMarkerFileReader`, `IAuthRotationHandler`), `McpServer.Repl.Host` (`AgentStdioHandler`)

technical.body:

All client operations SHALL support the generic passthrough pattern for extensibility.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Inside a hook, every REPL call's timeout is the lesser of its per-method timeout and the whole seconds left before the hook's deadline, and a call is not started when less than one second is left (it fails as timed out, so a persist keeps its write-ahead failsafe record as the fallback); the deadline is the hook process's start time plus the timeout the plugin's generated hooks.json registers for that hook, less a three-second margin for writing the hook's result; a hook with no registered timeout, and every call outside a hook, keeps the per-method timeouts unchanged. The deadline belongs only to a hook running in a process started for that hook (the process's command line names the hook's entry script under the plugin root, or the running plugin-hook.ps1 itself): a hook script run inside a process started for something else publishes no deadline, and every generated hook entry leaves MCP_HOOK_DEADLINE_UTC_MS and MCP_MEMORY_REPL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS as it found them when it returns, so calls made later in the same process keep their per-method timeouts (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D1, triage-report-124a374c; operator decision 2026-10-15 "Scope D1 to the hook process", after the plugin repositories' own ReplMethodTimeout and MemoryInjection tests failed on a deadline left in their Pester process; DeadlineAssertion_AcceptsMarginAndRejectsNoMargin, TimeoutCapAssertion_AcceptsCapAndRejectsUncapped, HookOwnershipAssertion_AcceptsOwnedEntriesAndRejectsForeignOrOtherHook, HookEnvironmentAssertion_AcceptsRestoredAndRejectsLeakedOrRemoved, HookDeadline_RegisteredTimeoutLessMargin_FromProcessStart and HookDeadline_NoRegisteredTimeout_NoDeadline (each run in a process started for the hook), HookOwnership_ShippedFunction_PinnedCommandLines, HookDeadline_ForeignProcess_PublishesNothing, HookEntry_InProcess_RestoresDeadlineAndMemoryTimeout, ReplTimeout_InsideHook_CappedByTimeLeft, ReplTimeout_OutsideHook_Unchanged).

A UserPromptSubmit hook whose server calls do not answer attempts its server call and returns before its registered timeout with the turn opened degraded and the write-ahead failsafe record kept, also when it must first supersede an in-progress turn; proven at the production UserPromptSubmit timeout of 10 s (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D1, triage-report-124a374c; BudgetAssertion_AcceptsDegradedWithinBudgetAndRejectsOverrun, UserPromptSubmit_UnansweredServer_OpensDegradedTurnWithinBudget).

technical.body:

Acceptance Criteria: (AC1) Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds returns >30 for analyzeRequirements/generateDocument and 30 for sessionlog methods; (AC2) REPL_TIMEOUT overrides the short default and REPL_LONG_TIMEOUT overrides the long budget; Invoke-ReplRaw uses Get-ReplMethodTimeoutSeconds. Origin: BUG-TRIAGE-072 (workflow.todo.analyzeRequirements, which blocks on an external Copilot CLI, was killed at the flat 30s REPL_TIMEOUT). Applied to plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 (canonical) and mcpserver-claude-code-plugin/lib. Validated by TEST-MCP-REPL-027.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-REPL-009; TEST: TEST-MCP-REPL-025, TEST-MCP-REPL-026, TEST-MCP-REPL-027, TEST-MCP-REPL-028

acceptanceCriteria.text: An invocation whose backend call succeeded drains the queue after the invoked method completes and its output is written, including an invocation that makes only one backend call; the drain never runs between two backend calls of one method, so beginTurn persists the superseded turn and the new turn before any queued record is replayed (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D1, triage-report-124a374c; ReplayOrderAssertion_AcceptsDrainLastAndRejectsDrainBetweenCalls, Drain_SingleCallInvocation_RunsAfterMethodOutput, Drain_BeginTurn_ReplaysQueueOnlyAfterTurnPersists).

Inside a hook the drain starts a record only while at least one second remains before the hook's deadline and caps each replay at the time left; records it does not reach stay queued with their attempt counts unchanged (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D1, triage-report-124a374c; DrainDeadlineAssertion_AcceptsStopAndRejectsDrainPastDeadline, Drain_InsideHookPastDeadline_LeavesRecordsQueuedUnattempted).

technical.body:
BUG-TRIAGE-097. The plugin PowerShell runtime captures every session-log submit into the failsafe queue before the remote call but never replays it, so records accumulate forever (33 on disk in F:/GitHub/McpServer, oldest 2026-07-14). plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST expose Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrain, which walks the failsafe directory oldest-first (the file name is prefixed with the UTC capture stamp, so a name sort is a chronological sort) and re-issues each record's captured method and params through Invoke-ReplRaw. A record MUST be deleted only after its submission succeeds; a record whose submission fails MUST stay on disk. client.SessionLog.SubmitAsync is an upsert keyed by sessionId plus requestId, so a replay is idempotent. A record rejected by the backend MUST NOT block the newer records behind it: the drain increments that record's drainAttempts counter and continues the walk. A transport-level failure (MCP_UNTRUSTED, mcpserver-repl not on PATH, timeout, refused connection) MUST abort the pass without consuming any attempt budget, because the backend and not the record is at fault. The drain MUST skip the record belonging to the submit currently in flight, so a drain triggered inside an active submit cannot double-submit or delete the live turn. The drain MUST be wired to the first successful Invoke-ReplRaw in the process (Invoke-ReplFailsafeDrainOnFirstSuccess, latched to run at most once and disabled by MCP_FAILSAFE_DRAIN_DISABLED=1) rather than to bootstrap: bootstrap only proves the marker file is fresh, does not prove the backend answers, and runs inside Invoke-ReplRaw, so draining there would recurse. Operators MUST be able to force a full pass with the plugin-local verb workflow.failsafe.drain (optional maxRecords and maxAttempts params), which prints the drain summary as YAML and exits non-zero only when the pass aborted.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-REPL-011; TEST: TEST-MCP-REPL-031, TEST-MCP-REPL-032, TEST-MCP-REPL-033, TEST-MCP-REPL-034, TEST-MCP-REPL-035, TEST-MCP-REPL-036, TEST-MCP-REPL-037, TEST-MCP-REPL-038, TEST-MCP-REPL-039
technical.title: Failsafe queue drains oldest-first after a proven-reachable backend call

technical.body:
BUG-TRIAGE-097. A failsafe record that cannot be replayed MUST be quarantined rather than retried forever or deleted, because a captured record can be the only copy of a turn. plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 MUST move a record to a quarantine subdirectory of the failsafe directory, next to a sibling .reason.txt naming the quarantine timestamp, the original path, and the reason, when the record is not readable YAML, when its root is not a mapping, when it has no method or no params, or when its drainAttempts counter has reached the attempt budget (default 5). Quarantined records MUST NOT be counted as live queue depth. plugins/core/lib-ps/resolve-cache-dir.ps1 MUST own the single resolution of the queue location (Get-McpFailsafeDir and Get-McpFailsafeQuarantineDir, honouring MCPSERVER_FAILSAFE_DIR then MCP_FAILSAFE_DIR then the workspace cache) so the writer, the drain, and the status reporter cannot disagree. plugins/core/lib-ps/mcp-status.ps1 MUST count the failsafe directory: pendingCount previously counted only the cache pending directory and therefore reported 0 while 33 captured submits sat undrained, so pendingCount MUST be the sum of pending turn records and queued failsafe records, and the status document MUST additionally expose pendingTurnCount, failsafeDir, failsafeCount, and failsafeQuarantineCount. A read-only workflow.failsafe.status verb MUST report the same depth without replaying anything.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-REPL-011; TEST: TEST-MCP-REPL-031, TEST-MCP-REPL-032, TEST-MCP-REPL-033, TEST-MCP-REPL-034, TEST-MCP-REPL-035, TEST-MCP-REPL-036, TEST-MCP-REPL-037, TEST-MCP-REPL-038, TEST-MCP-REPL-039
technical.title: Failsafe quarantine and truthful pending queue depth in plugin status

technical.body:
Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-087, 089, 091, 098, the PowerShell half of 090 and 094, and the PowerShell half of 101. plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 declares the turn-upsert Title parameter as [Parameter(Mandatory)][string] with no [AllowEmptyString()] at line 944, while callers deliberately pass an empty string per TR-MCP-REPL-015 so a stale cached title is not resubmitted. PowerShell rejects the bind before any request is made, so appendDialog without a queryTitle, appendActions, completeTurn, and the supersede path all fail with a mandatory-parameter binding error rather than persisting. The parameter SHALL accept an empty string, and every call path that legitimately passes one SHALL persist. Any other mandatory string parameter on the same path that would reject a legitimate empty value SHALL be corrected the same way. Pester coverage SHALL prove the binding failure before the fix and the successful persist after, using a temporary cache directory so no test touches the real workspace state.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-143; TEST: TEST-MCP-194, TEST-MCP-REPL-040

acceptanceCriteria.text: The supersede path chooses the canceled turn's title from the local cache alone, with no server read: a refined local title is sent, and a raw or empty local title (the prompt's first line or 'User prompt') is omitted, so the server keeps its stored title under the additive turn merge (FR-SUPPORT-015); raw prompt text is never sent (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 D1, triage-report-124a374c; SupersedeTitleAssertion_AcceptsLocalOnlyAndRejectsServerRead, SupersedeTitle_LocalCacheOnly_NoServerRead, 'TEST-MCP-REPL-040 supersede keeps a locally refined title without a server round trip', 'TEST-MCP-REPL-040 supersede omits a raw prompt-derived local title without a server read', 'TEST-MCP-REPL-040 supersede omits the title when the local default is raw and the server has none').

technical.body:
Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-086. Invoke-ReplSupersedeCurrentTurnIfInProgress in plugins/core/lib-ps/repl-invoke.ps1 reads queryTitle only from the local current-turn.yaml and then re-persists the canceled turn, so a title the agent refined server-side is overwritten by the stale local value and the session title is clobbered on every prompt. The hook cannot summarize, so it writes the prompt first line or the literal placeholder, which means the local copy is frequently the worse of the two. The supersede path SHALL prefer the server-side title when the local cache holds no title or holds only the hook's raw default, and SHALL never replace a refined title with raw prompt text. Coverage SHALL prove that a refined title survives a supersede and that a genuinely absent title still results in a persisted turn.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-143; TEST: TEST-MCP-194, TEST-MCP-REPL-040
technical.title: Supersede preserves a server-refined turn title

technical.body:
Implements FR-MCP-143 and closes BUG-TRIAGE-099. Plugin Status reports hasSession and hasCurrentTurn from the local cache (session-state.yaml carrying verified plus a non-empty sessionId, and the presence of current-turn.yaml), and the beginTurn path writes those files, but failTurn requires an empty in-process REPL state and otherwise returns "No active session exists". The result is that a turn the plugin reports as active cannot be closed as failed, so a wrap-up cannot truthfully record a validation failure and the turn is left in progress forever. failTurn SHALL resolve the active session and turn the same way the rest of the plugin does, falling back to the cache when the in-process state is empty, and SHALL close the turn as failed when the cache identifies one. Coverage SHALL prove the current refusal before the fix and a successful fail-close afterwards, using a temporary cache directory.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-143; TEST: TEST-MCP-194, TEST-MCP-REPL-040
technical.title: failTurn resolves the active turn from the plugin cache

acceptanceCriteria.text: The service canonicalizes and validates all IDs, scopes, acceptance criteria, operation uniqueness, delete targets, and final referential integrity before the first mutation.

One database transaction contains requirement rows, acceptance-criteria rows, mappings, deletions, idempotency state, and the recovery audit row; rollback restores the exact pre-state on every provider.
The effective-state hash is compared immediately before mutation, and the idempotency key is reserved and committed in the same transaction. Competing plans cannot both commit against one pre-state.
The operation planner orders mapping removals before target deletes and validates the final graph before commit while preserving canonical requirement and acceptance-criterion identifiers.
Server, typed client, REPL schema, shared plugin core, and every generated or copied plugin surface derive from one canonical request and result contract using object-first serialization.

The canonical precondition envelope includes workspace ID, target layer key, productScope, layer-catalog version or hash, scopeStartLayerKey, scopeEndLayerKey, sorted raw target-layer records including shadowed rows, and the sorted effective projection. Canonical UTF-8 JSON and SHA-256 produce deterministic plan and state hashes.

Inside the serializable provider transaction, the service locks or concurrency-checks the target layer and catalog metadata, revalidates raw and effective hashes, and rejects mutation of records not owned by the declared target layer or outside the declared scope bounds.
