technical.body:
# Linux Grok RunAs worker

## Status and exact goal

Proposed architecture, October 6, 2026. No worker implementation or deployment is claimed.

The operator's goal is a completed Agent Helper answer using deployed defaults,
with the actual Grok process running as `sharpninja`. The MCP process remains
`mcpserver`, with `NoNewPrivileges=true`. Merely setting HOME, binding options,
launching Grok, or obtaining an echo fallback does not satisfy the goal.

Authoritative proposed traceability captured October 6, 2026 through the active
Cline PowerShell plugin: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, TR-MCP-RUNAS-001 and
TEST-MCP-RUNAS-001. Supported Get/effective readbacks verify status proposed,
seven structured AC1-AC7 on each record, all isSatisfied=false, and the mapping.
This is requirements capture only, not implementation or deployment authorization.
Explicit operator approval of the architecture remains outstanding.

Durable proof (workspace-relative paths):
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/id-preflight.json - IDs absent before create; existing dependencies verified.
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/readback-Fr.yaml
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/readback-Tr.yaml
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/readback-Test.yaml
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/readback-mapping.yaml
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/effective-after.yaml
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/verification.json
- docs/receipts/runas-f6/session-proof.yaml

The RUNAS FR maps to RUNAS TR/TEST, TR-MCP-HELP-001/010,
TEST-MCP-HELP-004/005, TR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001 and
TEST-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001. Existing FR-MCP-HELP-001/010/011 and
FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001 are linked in record notes; their mappings/statuses
are unchanged. The mapping schema supports TR/TEST IDs, not FR dependencies.
Canonical docs/Project export was attempted through the supported client but
returned access denied; no direct-store edit, privilege bypass or retry.
Failure reported as triage-report-6875b680969f4ebb9a777c7ddf422ad2 with
failsafe and accepted triage receipts under docs/receipts/runas-f6/.

## Observed failure and boundary

The present Grok strategy uses `IProcessSpawner` in the server process.
`GrokCliAgentExecutionStrategy.RunPromptAsync` creates a server-owned prompt
file before spawning. Configurable RunAs cannot itself transfer Unix identity.
The existing service's `NoNewPrivileges=true` must not be weakened to permit
setuid sudo delegation. Authentication files must not be copied to mcpserver.

Source anchors:

- `/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer/src/McpServer.Services/Services/GrokCliAgentExecutionStrategy.cs`:
  `RunPromptAsync`, `BuildStartInfo`, `BuildGrokArgumentList`.
- `/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer/src/McpServer.Services/Services/AgentHelp/AgentHelpConversationService.cs`:
  `BuildAgentCliOptions` and `ExecuteHelperAsync`.
- `/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer/src/McpServer.Common.AgentCli/ProcessEnvironmentService.cs`:
  Linux environment behavior requires regression coverage, not identity claims.
- `/etc/systemd/system/mcpserver.service`: current service identity and hardening.

## Decision and authorization

Introduce a separate .NET worker running as sharpninja, reachable only by a
restricted Unix socket. This adds an administrator-installed service and is an
architectural change. Require explicit operator approval of this design before
product implementation. `fix it` authorizes remediation, but does not silently
approve every cross-account capability in a new architecture.

Rejected alternatives:

- HOME-only changes: do not change UID or securely grant credential access.
- Running the entire MCP server as sharpninja: unnecessarily broad identity change.
- Disabling NoNewPrivileges and permitting sudo: weakens existing server hardening.
- Copying API keys or login caches: duplicates private authentication material.

Security consequence: an authorized mcpserver process can ask an agent to act
with sharpninja's access to the allowed workspace. The worker is NOT a sandbox
for model tool calls. Socket authentication and workspace restrictions reduce
exposure but cannot eliminate this delegated trust. Operator approval includes
this consequence. Do not advertise arbitrary-code isolation.

## Scope and compatibility

- Add nullable `AgentHelp:RunAs` and `AgentHelp:WorkerSocketPath`, with matching
  `AgentCliClientOptions` routing information where necessary.
- Preserve existing `TodoPromptOptions.RunAs` fallback when AgentHelp.RunAs is
  unset. Explicit AgentHelp.RunAs takes precedence. No session-level identity
  override and no untrusted network selection of worker users.
- Linux nonempty RunAs must use the configured worker, fail closed on identity
  mismatch/unavailability, and never silently execute under the server UID.
- Empty Linux RunAs retains current local Grok execution. Windows retains its
  existing profile/process-launch behavior.
- Initially support Agent Helper one-shot Grok execution only. Voice, TODO,
  triage, persistent QuadBrain sessions, other strategies, and brain-slot
  migration are not silently included in this slice.
- No public HTTP response schema break. New deployment components and optional
  settings are additive. Existing Linux users relying on ineffective RunAs
  now receive a clear failure rather than false impersonation.

## Worker interface

Use built-in .NET Unix-domain sockets and System.Text.Json, not new libraries.
New project: `/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer/src/McpServer.GrokWorker/`.
Share versioned transport contracts in the existing Common.AgentCli project.
Add a dedicated `IAgentHelpExecutionRouter`, injected only into
AgentHelpConversationService. Do not select the worker inside the shared Grok
strategy, or infer helper purpose from generic AgentCliClientOptions.RunAs.
The helper router selects remote one-shot execution only for Linux, nonempty
effective helper RunAs, and the grok-cli strategy. It rejects another selected
strategy when RunAs is configured, including explicit session overrides.
Local helper execution still delegates to the existing strategy resolver.
Voice, TODO, triage and persistent sessions never receive this router; tests
exercise each excluded caller with generic RunAs set and prove no worker call.
This slice does not fix identity switching in those excluded callers, and must
not claim that it does. No shell, sudo, pkexec, or arbitrary command string is
accepted by the protocol.

One connection owns one invocation. Four-byte unsigned big-endian length
followed by UTF-8 JSON frames; protocol version 1; reject malformed lengths,
unknown versions, duplicate invocation IDs and unknown fields. Initial request:
invocation UUID, requested user, prompt text, workspace identifier, optional
model and requested timeout. Client cannot supply executable, prompt path,
HOME, environment map, arbitrary CLI flags, UID/GID, or filesystem outputs.

Reply events: started (actual UID, account, worker PID, child PID), stdout,
stderr, and exactly one terminal result (exit code, error category, canceled
flag, cleanup success). Correlate every event with invocation UUID. Preserve
stdout/stderr callbacks and AgentCliResult semantics. Logs include correlation
and identity, not prompts, tokens or full authentication-related stderr.

Enforce limits before allocation: initial request <= 1 MiB, output event <=
64 KiB, accumulated stdout and stderr <= 4 MiB each, one active invocation,
handshake <= 10 seconds, effective run timeout <= 120 seconds. UTF-8 byte
limits are tested with multibyte input. Excess output terminates the process
and returns an explicit resource-limit error, never a completed answer.

Client disconnect, cancellation, timeout, EndAsync and DisposeAsync all close
the invocation and require worker cancellation of the whole child process tree.
No detached background job survives an invocation. Use process-tree kill,
bounded drain/wait, and systemd KillMode=control-group on worker shutdown.
Lifecycle tests must prove cleanup; a timeout is not treated as completion.

## Revision 2: decisions addressing independent review F1-F5

This revision is a design proposal, not approval or implemented behavior.
The original failed review remains immutable. F6 authoritative requirement
persistence is now evidenced by the supported readbacks above; the canonical
markdown export is separately blocked by access denied. U1-U3 and approval,
implementation and deployed-helper acceptance remain unverified.

### F2: per-invocation OS lifetime, not ancestry-only kill

Replace the preceding process-tree-kill proposal with a dedicated transient
service in sharpninja's systemd user manager for each invocation. Use the
installed systemd-run executable via ArgumentList, with fixed --user, --pipe,
--wait, --quiet, --service-type=exec, --expand-environment=no, and generated UUID
unit name. Never combine --pipe with --remain-after-exit. The fixed command is
the root-owned published worker executable in invocation-runner mode, not Grok
directly. No client may choose unit names, commands, modes or unit properties.
The runner launches only the policy-pinned Grok with existing argument contract.
It is the unit main process and remains alive until explicitly stopped; Grok is
its child. Configure ExitType=main, RemainAfterExit=no, KillMode=control-group,
SendSIGKILL=yes, TimeoutStartSec=10s, TimeoutStopSec=5s, Restart=no,
RuntimeMaxSec=(requested timeout + 15 seconds), NoNewPrivileges=yes and
CollectMode=inactive. The runner never calls sd_notify to extend timeouts.

Handshake and capture protocol, including immediate Grok exits:
1. Before launch persist UUID/unit name, worker epoch, private prompt directory,
   launch monotonic timestamp and deadline. Refuse a pre-existing unit. The
   runner receives only generated identifiers and the root-owned policy path;
   prompt/config data travel over framed redirected stdin, not command arguments.
2. The runner validates its actual UID, UUID and /proc/self/cgroup, sends a ready
   frame containing PID, UID and canonical cgroup path, and blocks for start ACK.
   The worker queries manager MainPID, InvocationID and ControlGroup, checks the
   ready frame matches the actual active unit, persists the matching identity,
   then sends start plus validated prompt/model/deadline. NO Grok process may be
   launched before this handshake. Runner startup/no-ACK deadline is 10 seconds.
   Missing/pruned cgroup or unit before ACK is a failed launch, never success.
3. Runner creates private prompt files, launches Grok, drains stdout and stderr
   concurrently into bounded frames and waits for actual Grok exit. It reports
   the Grok exit code separately from the runner/systemd-run exit. Following
   child exit it stays alive, continuously awaiting stop or local deadline; this
   pins its cgroup and keeps RuntimeMaxSec effective in running state. Descendant
   output pipes never gate exit observation; bounded drains continue independently.
4. Worker persists the correlated child-exit frame then stops the exact unit
   through systemctl --user. The runner deliberately does not self-exit on normal
   child success before stop, and there is no active-exited retention dependency.
   SIGTERM/SIGKILL may terminate it during cleanup; manager or launcher exit codes
   caused by this intentional stop are not substituted for the Grok exit code.
5. Wait for stop, bounded launcher exit and stream drain; verify the previously
   observed cgroup has populated=0 recursively or its canonical directory no
   longer exists after completed stop. Directory absence is not success unless
   identity was captured before ACK and stop completed; PID/EOF/unit-not-found
   alone are not proof. Read errors fail cleanup. Worker removes its owned private
   prompt directory after verified stop, including crash paths. Persist receipts
   before accepting child status 0 plus FINAL ANSWER as completed.

Starting, queries and ambiguous launch are bounded: ready/ACK budget 10 seconds
from launch; every manager query <=2 seconds; local child deadline starts at ACK
and is <=120 seconds; stop/cgroup confirmation <=10 seconds; final drain <=5
seconds. On an ambiguous launcher/start/query timeout, cancel the launcher and
stop the persisted exact unit name (even if PID unknown), verify no pending start
job and absent/empty unit cgroup before admission resumes. If manager observation
fails, report failure and become unhealthy; killing systemd-run is not cleanup.
An unresolved manager job prevents successful cleanup. Recovery sweeps generated
units and pending jobs before listening. No completion without identity evidence.

Independent crash bound: Type=exec start budget 10s, running budget <=135s,
stop budget 5s: <=150 seconds from unit start-job execution, assuming a responsive
manager/kernel. Queued job scheduling is not a hard real-time bound; no ACK means
no Grok, and startup recovery handles the persisted pending job. The runner holds
the running state after Grok exits, so manager expiry still stops all cooperative
descendants if the worker dies after child exit. If runner dies, ExitType=main
starts cgroup shutdown immediately. User manager failure is outside independent
timer guarantees, fails health and requires operator recovery; never claim cleanup.
Transport EOF also triggers runner cancellation, but is not the sole guarantee.

Red/integration coverage must exercise hundreds of immediate child zero/nonzero
exits, pre-ACK failures, delayed status observation, leftover descendants and
inherited pipes, worker crash after child exit, runner crash, start/query hangs,
ambiguous jobs, manager loss, unreadable cgroups and output overflow. Record UID,
matching pre-ACK cgroup, child status and actual bounded cleanup independently.

Runner control transport uses the same bounded framing as the worker socket,
with internal ready/start/child-exit types and strict UUID/epoch correlation.
Only runner stdout carries framed events; Grok stdout/stderr are redirected by
the runner and encoded separately, never inherited directly into control stdout.
Drain systemd-run stderr independently as bounded launcher diagnostics; --quiet
does not make stderr a control channel. Runner verifies parent-issued start
frame exactly once, rejects unknown fields and applies independent startup,
child-run and frame deadlines. The worker must observe both actual Grok UID and
runner UID in started receipts; runner UID alone is not process-identity proof.
Output caps count actual UTF-8 payload bytes independently of frame overhead.
Launcher disconnect/EOF before start causes runner exit without Grok; after start
it requests cancellation and relies on unit shutdown as the containment boundary.

The worker continuously drains both pipe streams into bounded queues independent
of the client. On cancellation or transport loss it calls systemctl --user stop
for the exact generated unit and waits at most 10 seconds for stop plus empty
cgroup. At most 5 seconds may be spent on output drain. Cleanup failure returns
an error and makes the worker unhealthy; no next invocation is admitted.
Never interpret disappearance of the root PID, EOF or launcher exit alone as
proof of full cleanup. Terminal success requires the recorded Grok exit status,
both stream limits respected, the invocation cgroup empty and private files gone.

On worker crash the user manager independently enforces the runner RuntimeMaxSec plus the
stop timeout. Cleanup after crash is therefore bounded, not instantaneous. A
replacement worker sweeps only its generated-prefix units and own prompt dirs
before listening. First-install preflight must verify cgroup v2, user-manager
connectivity and permission to start/query/stop transient units without sudo.
Linger is currently disabled on this system. Nuke must snapshot and enable
sharpninja lingering, preserve user-manager ownership, and restore its prior
state on rollback; this is an explicit additional deployment side effect.

Containment is a lifecycle mechanism for cooperative Grok subprocesses, not a
sandbox preventing a malicious sharpninja process from requesting other units
or moving itself. Authentication and executable trust remain as disclosed above.
Integration gates include normal exit with leftover descendants, double fork,
reparenting, inherited pipes, disconnect, timeout, worker kill/restart, manager
unavailability and cleanup failure. Fail a test if a recorded child survives the
specified deadline, even when helper text is otherwise valid.

### F3: connection admission, replay and backpressure

Listener backlog is 8; application admits at most 8 authenticated connections,
including handshake/invocation/reply states, and exactly one active invocation.
There is no invocation queue. An idle capacity-excess or busy peer is closed
immediately; an optional bounded error reply gets at most 1 second. Authenticate
SO_PEERCRED before parsing any bytes. Handshake deadline is 10 seconds measured
from accept, not restarted for partial reads. A frame read or write has a
5-second absolute deadline. Only one outstanding 64-KiB event per connection
is buffered for outbound delivery; stop reading Grok output into unbounded memory.
Stdout/stderr are drained independently with the existing 4-MiB-per-stream cap.
If the outbound consumer stalls, cancel the invocation rather than buffer more.
Terminal reply/drain gets 5 seconds; its failure must not prevent cancellation.

Retain at most 4096 invocation UUIDs for 10 minutes, including failed launches.
Evict expired entries, but never evict a live entry. If capacity remains full,
reject new work. Restart loses replay history; document IDs as per-worker-epoch
at-most-once, not globally exactly-once. Started events include a worker epoch.
Flood, partial-frame, invalid-length, repeated UUID, multibyte-limit and
non-reading-client tests must prove bounded memory, admission and cleanup.

### F4: fail-closed compatibility and authentication preflight

Validate remote-helper inputs before sending any prompt. Reject configured
ModelApiKey, any nonempty session AgentParameters/environment map, and session
AgentPath overrides other than the exact pinned policy path. Do not silently
drop these fields or send secrets across accounts. Error messages name the
incompatible option without its value. An override equal to the pinned path is
accepted; omitted path uses the pinned path. Models are auto or a policy-allowed
ID; reject others. RunAs must resolve to the policy's exact sharpninja UID.
Other strategies with effective RunAs fail closed. Local/Windows options retain
their current semantics and regression tests.

Remote timeouts must be finite and positive, at most 120 seconds. Reject zero,
negative, infinite and over-limit values rather than silently changing semantics.
Environment is server-policy-only: HOME=/home/sharpninja,
XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS pointing to that user's
bus, and an administrator-fixed PATH containing the verified install and system
binaries. Set these fixed environment values explicitly on EVERY transient
invocation unit through administrator-controlled systemd-run ArgumentList; do
The helper-only slice does not accept optional environment files. Each invocation
sets explicit --setenv=NAME=VALUE arguments for HOME, USER=sharpninja,
LOGNAME=sharpninja, XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS and fixed PATH.
The worker's ProcessStartInfo environment only connects systemd-run/systemctl
to the user manager; it does not establish the transient service environment.
Use --property=WorkingDirectory=/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer and
--property=UMask=0077 on every unit. No shell, no argument-variable expansion,

### F5: journaled Nuke transaction for MCP plus worker

Extend Nuke, not ad hoc copying. Acquire an exclusive host deployment lock before
staging or inspecting mutable live state; refuse a second deployment. Save a
root-owned transaction manifest and flush it atomically before each side effect.
Back up both complete published trees, hashes and deployment manifests; the
MCP/worker service units and drop-ins; the worker socket unit; policy and live
YAML; active/enabled/masked states; socket metadata; and sharpninja's linger state.
Database/data directories are not replaced or rolled back by this transaction.
Quiesce work before the snapshot and leave unrelated data intact.

Persist these states: Prepared -> Quiesced -> WorkerInstalled -> WorkerVerified
-> McpInstalled -> HelperVerified -> Committed. Any exception or interrupted
noncommitted journal enters Recovering and must reach RolledBack or RecoveryFailed.
At each state retain the exact backups and installed hashes needed to reverse
all mutations. The existing updater's configuration-only recovery is explicitly
insufficient; implement and failure-injection-test binary recovery first.

Quiesce by stopping MCP admission/service, stopping worker socket admission, then
worker and outstanding generated invocation units. Confirm empty cgroups before
replacement. Preserve and reject preexisting masked units unless the operator
explicitly authorizes unmasking. Publish/install worker and policy first, reload
units, start socket then worker, verify peer restriction, UID, Grok authentication
and cleanup. Only then install MCP and object-mutate its preserved helper keys.
Start MCP and run a defaults-only helper answer before committing the journal.

Rollback stops new MCP, socket, worker and generated invocation units; confirms
cleanup; restores old trees/manifests/policy/config/units/drop-ins; removes only
transaction-created units/files when previously absent; reloads systemd; restores
masked/enabled/active state and linger state. Start restored worker socket/service
only when previously active, then restored MCP when previously active. Verify
prior binary hashes and health. Never report full rollback if only YAML or MCP
health was restored. If cleanup or restoration fails, leave admission stopped,
retain backups, report RecoveryFailed and require administrator intervention.

Inject failure and restart at every persisted transition, including after worker
success but MCP/helper failure, after first-install unit creation, after config
mutation and during recovery. An incomplete journal is recovered before another
update. An operator-visible helper acceptance failure always keeps the original
goal open, even when prior service health is successfully restored.

## Byrd v4 slices and gates

1. Requirements and architectural design: capture FR/TR/TEST/AC and mapping;
   independently review security boundary, compatibility, full plan and approval.
2. Red tests: options forwarding, local/remote selection, identity mismatch,
   peer rejection, frame limits, cancellation/tree cleanup, prompt ownership,
   secret-safe diagnostics and updater preservation/rollback. Use mocks only
   for unit scope. Run the tests and retain expected failures before coding.
   Independent review of AC coverage before implementation.
3. Green implementation: configuration, framing/client, worker, remote session,
   Nuke deployment. Run full current and prior unit suite with zero failures
   and zero skips; remediate existing suite blockers rather than filtering them
   out for phase acceptance. Independent review before leaving implementation.
4. Integration: real Unix socket and separate UIDs, negative authorization,
   process identity, owned prompt files and termination on disconnect. Retain
   process/UID and exit receipts. No fake strategy can prove impersonation.
5. Deployment acceptance: Nuke via pkexec, verify service health and both units,
   call Agent Helper without RunAs/path/model/strategy session overrides, and
   require status completed plus expected FINAL ANSWER content from real Grok.
   Correlate helper turn with worker started/exit events proving sharpninja UID;
   verify MCP UID=mcpserver and NoNewPrivileges=true throughout. Independent
   review with accuracy and completeness >=98 before any done-state change.

Every review requires durable request and full response JSONL and the entire

technical.body: CORRECTED 2026-07-20 after the original specification was proven wrong by test. Context unchanged: trusted parties and their keys live in the TransactionSecurity key store (KeyServerPartyEntity, KeyServerPartyKeyEntity), a separate SQLite database created with EnsureCreated, so the McpDbContext Creativity/Logic rename migration cannot reach them; BrainSlotRegistryService.RegisterPartyAsync registers the party only and never a key, while ValidateReadinessAsync requires an active signing key at "{partyId}:signing:1". On any migrated installation the renamed party therefore starts with no key and the quad reports NotReady. WHAT WAS WRONG: the first version of this requirement said to COPY the legacy party's signing key material forward. That is impossible and harmful. PartyKeyDescriptor and KeyServerPartyKeyEntity expose only PublicKeyPem, so only the public half can ever be read; InMemoryKeyServerService retains a private ECDsa handle only for a pair it generated itself, and CreateSigningKey given a public PEM with no private PEM stores an empty private-key set. The result passed every readiness gate and could never sign: turn transactions were rejected with TransactionFailureReason.UnknownKey after the model provider had already been invoked and billed, and persisting that row also suppressed TurnTransactionCoordinator.EnsureDefaultPartiesAsync, which mints a working pair only when no key row exists. CORRECT BEHAVIOR: when a brain slot's party has no active signing key and a legacy party id exists (brain-slot:left-hemisphere for Creativity, brain-slot:right-hemisphere for Logic), the runtime SHALL register the renamed party with NO key material so the keyserver mints a fresh pair and retains its private half, and SHALL leave the legacy party and key rows untouched. Historical verification is unaffected because a manifest carries its own PublisherPartyId and VerifyManifestAsync resolves the public key from that legacy party. Reconciliation remains idempotent, is a no-op when the new key already exists or no legacy party is found, and never rotates an existing key. Proven by TEST-MCP-192 and by BrainSlotAdoptedPartyKeySigningTests, which now assert a committed turn transaction under the renamed party and continued verification of a legacy-signed manifest.
technical.title: Brain-slot signing keys follow a renamed party id

Mocks-first tests and full applicable unit suites pass with zero failures/skips; independent gates pass; existing local Linux service update preserves configuration/data and trusted workspace behavior.

Every case of the build's service-update infrastructure tests runs and passes on Linux and on Windows with no skip. A case whose Linux check needs a Linux-only facility (a FIFO, Unix file modes, GNU tar ACL and xattr preservation, unlinking a directory symbolic link with File.Delete) asserts on Windows the outcome the helper produces there for the same input (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 C2, triage-report-cdf116ad, as BUG-BASELINE-004 did for Windows-only tests; the stat double's FIFO case and the Windows cases of the Linux preflight, archive and replacement checks, which cite this criterion).

The Linux update reads a unit whose systemctl show output repeats a property on separate lines (systemd 262 prints one EnvironmentFiles line per environment file) and validates and preserves every environment file those lines name. Redeploy of 2026-11-04: on systemd 262 the update stopped at the second EnvironmentFiles line before any service change. Added under the operator's standing word of 2026-10-26: "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval".

After the start, the Linux update keeps checking HTTP health while the unit stays active, for up to 10 minutes, because the server registers every workspace before it listens (93 s on 2026-11-04 at 14:27); it fails as soon as the unit leaves the active state or the 10 minutes are spent, and never stops a unit that is still starting within them. Redeploy of 2026-11-04: an 18 s health window stopped a server that was starting normally. Added under the operator's standing word of 2026-10-26: "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval"; operator 2026-11-04: "Start now, fix target after (Recommended)".

When a Linux update fails after it has replaced the installed files, its recovery restores the preserved live state and then leaves the unit startable: a unit file or drop-in that names the legacy apphost McpServer.Support.Mcp is retargeted at QBrainAi.Support.Mcp, the apphost the completed replacement put in the install, as a successful update does, and systemd is reloaded after that change; a unit that already names QBrainAi.Support.Mcp is restored unchanged with no extra reload. The update still performs no binary rollback, and a failure before the replacement completes is outside this criterion. Redeploy of 2026-11-04: the failure path restored a unit file naming the removed legacy apphost, and the service could not start until a manual retarget. Fifth holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding d3; operator 2026-11-04: "Strengthen + fix in Z3 (Recommended)".

The Nuke UpdateService target publishes QBrainAi.Support.Mcp as ReadyToRun on both Windows and Linux by setting PublishReadyToRun=true on each RID-specific service DotNetPublish operation before deployment. The launcher publish is unchanged.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The vendor step expects the tarball file name npm pack derives from plugins/core/lib-node/package.json (the name with a scope's leading @ dropped and its / turned into -, then -<version>.tgz), refuses a manifest without a name, and fails the sync when npm pack reports a different file name, so renaming the package does not stop the sync (BUG-BUILD-010; proved by the build's pack-name infrastructure tests, which cite this criterion).

After the vendor step copies the packed plugin core into a consumer's vendor/sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core.tgz and rewrites its package.json reference, it refreshes that consumer's package-lock.json through npm. For a consumer whose package.json already referenced that stable tarball name before the sync (mcpserver-cline-plugin, mcpserver-cline-v2-plugin and mcpserver-opencode-plugin), the lockfile entry of the dependency its package.json names for the vendored tarball records the new tarball's SHA-512 integrity, package.json and every other lockfile line stay unchanged, and npm ci then succeeds without EINTEGRITY, also when the tarball's own package name differs from that dependency name (the core packs as @qbrainai/qbrain-ai-plugin-core while those consumers depend on @sharpninja/mcpserver-plugin-core). A plain npm install --package-lock-only leaves the stale integrity, and installing the bare file: spec adds a second dependency under the tarball's package name, so neither satisfies this; nothing but npm writes the lockfile (triage-report-de98c84b and -f2684f90, BUG-BASELINE-012; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E1; proved by the build's Node vendor lockfile infrastructure tests, a mock gate then bindings, which cite this criterion).

SyncAgentPlugins' version bump changes a Node plugin's package.json and package-lock.json only through npm, versioning each plugin root that has a package.json with npm version <next> --no-git-tag-version --allow-same-version --ignore-scripts: package.json changes in its version line only, package-lock.json in its two version lines only, no other character is re-escaped (an em dash, &&, + and >= stay as written), the vendored core's integrity is unchanged, and git gets no commit or tag; the bump writes plugin.json manifests and .version itself and never writes package.json or package-lock.json (triage-report-de98c84b and -f2684f90, BUG-BASELINE-012, operator ruling 2026-10-10 "Never edit an npm lockfile. It belongs to npm. If you want it changed, use npm."; PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 E1; found in the C3 sync of 2026-10-15, where the bump re-serialized all three lockfiles; proved by the build's Node vendor lockfile infrastructure tests, a mock gate then bindings, and its build-target test of the plugin version bump plan, which cite this criterion).

technical.body:
SyncAgentPlugins SHALL vendor the packed Node plugin core into consumer repositories under the version-less stable file name sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core.tgz, and SHALL NOT embed a package version in any vendored tarball file name or in the constant that names it. Rationale, from triage-report-52e8098cd299475d9922098f00d818b6: Build.SyncAgentPlugins.cs:465 hard-coded sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core-0.1.0.tgz while package.json had moved to 0.2.0 after a breaking-change bump, so the three Node plugin repositories held tarballs whose file name claimed the pre-breaking-change surface while their content was the new package; the versioned name is also why the constant existed at all, since consumer package.json files reference the tarball path and a version bump would break the reference. The vendor step SHALL discover consumer vendor directories by matching any sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core*.tgz variant so first-run migration finds the legacy versioned files, copy the packed artifact to the stable name, delete superseded variants from the vendor directory, and rewrite the consumer package.json dependency reference file:vendor/sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core*.tgz to the stable name via a targeted in-place replacement that preserves the file's formatting. The step SHALL also assert that npm pack produced a tarball whose embedded version matches plugins/core/lib-node/package.json, so a silent pack-versus-manifest drift fails the sync instead of shipping.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-MCP-143; TEST: TEST-MCP-194, TEST-MCP-REPL-040
technical.title: Node core vendor package uses a version-less stable file name

The authoritative store SHALL preserve projection metadata needed to rehydrate ordered sections, `code-review-remediation` phases, `notes`, `completed`, and the code-review reference without treating YAML as runtime source of truth.
Projection failures after a committed authoritative mutation SHALL surface an explicit failure result instead of silent success. technical.body:
TODO create, update, delete, and bootstrap-import operations SHALL append reconstructable audit snapshots with monotonic per-item versions. The server SHALL expose `GET /mcpserver/todo/{id}/audit` together with typed client parity and MCP STDIO tool parity so callers can retrieve ordered tracked states for a TODO item even when the current row has been deleted but audit history still exists.
Mutation results SHALL include a machine-readable failure classification so callers can distinguish validation, not-found, projection-failure, conflict, and external-sync error shapes when TODO operations fail or only partially succeed. For database-backed TODO storage (the authoritative mode per TR-MCP-TODO-005), a projection failure SHALL preserve committed authoritative database state, record operator-visible projection failure metadata, and leave `TODO.yaml` repairable without replaying the mutation. The server SHALL expose `GET /mcpserver/todo/projection/status` and `POST /mcpserver/todo/projection/repair` together with typed client parity and MCP STDIO tool parity so operators can verify whether `TODO.yaml` matches authoritative database state and rebuild it on demand.


**Covered by:** `ITodoService`, `ITodoStore`, `EfTodoService`, `TodoAuditHistoryEntity`, `TodoYamlFileSerializer`, `TodoController`, `McpServerMcpTools`, `TodoClient`, `TodoModels`, `TodoCreationService`, `TodoUpdateService`

technical.body:
When TR-MCP-TODO-005 provider-agnostic storage is enabled and a pre-existing legacy `mcp.db` SQLite TODO store is present at the deprecated `Mcp:TodoStorage:SqliteDataSource` path, the server SHALL copy rows from `todo_items`, `todo_item_history`, and `todo_document_metadata` into the configured authoritative database on first boot, preserving primary keys, audit identifiers, and monotonic per-item versions. The migrator SHALL be idempotent: subsequent starts SHALL be no-ops when the target TODO tables are non-empty or the completion marker file exists in the effective data folder. The migrator SHALL honor the `Mcp:TodoStorage:MigrateFromLegacySqlite` feature flag and SHALL run as a background hosted service so it never blocks the SCM 30-second service-start window. Failures SHALL log per-row context and continue with the next row rather than aborting the whole migration.

**Note:** In practice the provider-agnostic rewrite (TR-MCP-TODO-005) was shipped alongside the workspace-scoped schema (TR-MCP-TODO-008), whose per-workspace YAML bootstrap (`TodoBootstrapImporter`) replaces the need for a legacy `mcp.db` row copy. Live Phase 5 deploys on LEGION2 and PAYTON-DESKTOP (2026-04-21) reconstructed authoritative state from workspace YAML directly; legacy SQLite TODO rows are out-of-band archived to CSV when present (see `C:\Users\Public\mcpserver-postgres-archive-20260421` on PAYTON for the postgres/SQLite snapshot archived during deploy).

**Covered by:** `TodoBootstrapImporter` (replaces legacy migrator), per-workspace YAML bootstrap path
technical.title: Legacy SQLite TODO Storage One-Shot Migration

technical.body:
Database-backed TODO storage (TR-MCP-TODO-005) SHALL scope every TODO row, audit-history row, and document-metadata row to the active workspace via a `WorkspaceId` column populated from the resolved `WorkspaceContext.WorkspacePath`, matching the TR-MCP-MT-003 multi-tenant pattern used by context, session-log, agent, tool, and graph entities. `McpDbContext` SHALL install a global query filter on all three Todo entities so reads, updates, and deletes never cross workspace boundaries. `TodoItemEntity` SHALL use composite primary key `(WorkspaceId, Id)` so the same canonical TODO id MAY exist in multiple workspaces without collision. `TodoDocumentMetadataEntity` SHALL use composite primary key `(WorkspaceId, SingletonId = 1)` so each workspace owns exactly one document-metadata singleton. `TodoAuditHistoryEntity` SHALL carry `WorkspaceId` as a filter column and index; the audit primary key remains `(TodoId, Version)` scoped implicitly by the query filter.
Bootstrap SHALL import from the per-workspace `TodoFilePath` YAML into the authoritative database when that workspace's TODO rows are empty, running exactly once per workspace per marker-file lifetime. The bootstrap path SHALL preserve ordered sections, completed items, notes, code-review reference, and projection metadata identically to the single-workspace bootstrap shape used by `TodoService`. After bootstrap, YAML projection SHALL write to the workspace-specific `TodoFilePath`; no other workspace's YAML SHALL be touched.

The `LegacyTodoSqliteMigrator` (TR-MCP-TODO-007) SHALL stamp imported rows with the active workspace's `WorkspacePath`. REST routes `/mcpserver/todo/*` and MCP STDIO `todo_*` tools SHALL honor the workspace resolved by the existing `WorkspaceAuthMiddleware` / `X-Workspace` header path without additional caller changes beyond what TR-MCP-MT-003 already mandates.


**Note:** Phase 5 live deploy verified on 2026-04-21: LEGION2 bootstrapped 130 items across 7 workspaces; PAYTON-DESKTOP bootstrapped 96 items across 5 workspaces (workspace scoping confirmed via `TodoBootstrapImporter summary` log lines with per-workspace `Imported:N` outcomes).

**Covered by:** `TodoItemEntity`, `TodoAuditHistoryEntity`, `TodoDocumentMetadataEntity`, `McpDbContext` (query filters + composite keys), `EfTodoService`, `TodoBootstrapImporter`, `TodoServiceFactory.CreateForWorkspace`, per-provider migration assemblies

technical.body:
Implements FR-MCP-141 and extends TR-MCP-TUN-003, which already establishes that NgrokTunnelProvider manipulates child-process environment variables. NgrokTunnelProvider SHALL take IProcessEnvironmentService and apply the interactive user's USERPROFILE, HOME, APPDATA, and PATH to the ProcessStartInfo of the ngrok child process, so ngrok.yml resolves when the server runs under LocalSystem instead of the provider silently starting with the service account profile. The provider SHALL resolve the ngrok binary through ResolveExecutable against that enriched PATH rather than relying on the literal string ngrok. When the binary cannot be found the provider SHALL log at Warning rather than Error, and the message SHALL name the Windows-service and Store-alias causes and the available remedies. Recovered from origin/claude/busy-dubinsky. Note that develop ships Tunnel Provider empty and Ngrok.Enabled false, so this path is dormant under stock configuration.

acceptanceCriteria.text: On Linux with Landlock, a missing export root (with its missing ancestors) and missing nested export folders are created on a thread Landlock-confined to the pinned root or, for a missing root, its deepest existing ancestor (pinned from its approved mount without following links or crossing mounts); a parent moved outside before mkdirat is refused by the kernel and nothing appears outside (BUG-BASELINE-001; BugTriage139EighteenthLinuxTests EnsureDirectory_MissingNestedDirectory_IsCreatedUnderLandlock, EnsureDirectory_ParentMovedOutsideBeforeCreate_IsDeniedByLandlock, OpenExportRoot_MissingRootAndAncestors_IsCreatedUnderLandlock, LandlockConfinement_DeniesDirectoryCreationOutsideItsHierarchy).

On Linux with Landlock, nested stale files and empty directories are deleted on a thread Landlock-confined to the root through the pinned parent after the target kind and identity match; a missing parent or target returns false; a parent moved outside before unlinkat is refused by the kernel and the entry survives; export cleanup deletes nested stale files (BUG-BASELINE-001; DeleteFileIfExists_NestedStaleFile_DeletesUnderLandlock, DeleteFileIfExists_NestedParentMovedOutsideBeforeUnlink_IsDeniedByLandlock, RequirementsExport_NestedStaleCleanup_DeletesStaleUnderLandlock).

On Linux without Landlock the export fails closed as before: missing roots and nested folders throw DirectoryNotFoundException before any mutation and nested stale cleanup is refused before any generated write (BUG-BASELINE-001; EnsureDirectory_MissingNestedDirectory_FailsClosedBeforeMutation, OpenExportRoot_MissingRoot_FailsClosedWithoutLandlock, RequirementsExport_NestedStaleCleanup_IsRejectedBeforeGeneratedWrite).

If the Landlock confinement cannot be established (ruleset creation, the path-beneath rule, no_new_privs, or restrict_self fails), the confined operation never runs and the call fails with an IOException, so no export mutation happens without kernel enforcement (BUG-BASELINE-001 what-if; BugTriage139EighteenthLinuxTests.LandlockConfinement_RuleSetupFailure_NeverRunsTheOperation, where the kernel rejects directory rights on a regular-file descriptor).

A symbolic link planted at a missing export folder name before mkdirat is never followed: mkdirat reports EEXIST, the re-open beneath the anchor refuses the link, the call fails, and nothing is created through the link outside the root (BUG-BASELINE-001 what-if; BugTriage139EighteenthLinuxTests.EnsureDirectory_SymlinkPlantedAtMissingSegment_IsNeverFollowed).

Every supported platform executes an applicable native contract assertion: a platform-specific test is a Category=Integration test tagged Platform=Linux or Platform=Windows for the host it applies to, which TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-1 and AC-2 route to that host's MigrationIntegrationTests and require to run and pass there, and it passes only as TR-MCP-USECASE-019 AC-008 states (operator 2026-10-30: "D3: dedupe lane rules (Recommended)"); no unit test depends on the platform or on the process environment, directly, through a test helper or through the production code it calls: a test whose outcome can change with the value of an environment variable it reads or writes, directly, through a test helper or through the production code it calls (for example a temporary-folder lookup that takes its folder from a variable and creates it), a test that imports the process environment into configuration (AddEnvironmentVariables or a default host builder), and a test that asserts on an environment value a child process inherits are Category=Integration tests that set and restore every variable their assertions or the code they call depend on, every name of a fallback chain the code reads, both forms where a variable has a canonical (QBrainAi, QBRAINAI_) and a legacy (Mcp, MCP_) form, and the tests that write the process environment run one at a time (operator 2026-10-21: "Fix both, strengthen ACs", "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "Approve, strengthen AC-006/008 (Recommended)"; operator 2026-10-26: "Strengthen AC, move 14 (Recommended)", "Dependence + proof AC (Recommended)" and "Fix source, strengthen AC (Recommended)"; hostile validation findings R5-F2, R6-F1 and R7-F1). The hostile-environment runs are out of scope: they are not part of this criterion or its evidence (operator 2026-10-27: "Get ride of the hostile runs enforcing integration test separation.  I have already stated this once." and "Which I sated last night were out of scope."). An integration case may read the lane's own inputs without setting them: MCP_REPOSITORY_ROOT, the MCP_TEST_ connection variables the lane provisions, and, for an import that scans agent folders, the user's real profile folder, read only and never asserted on; every other variable its assertions or the code it calls depend on it sets and restores. A unit test asserts no wall-clock bound (operator 2026-10-29: "Environment ACs (Recommended)"; holistic review findings MCPT-11, SVC-6 and MCPT-12). These rules are stated here once for TR-MCP-USECASE-019 AC-008 as well; the environment-delta rule moved to FR-MCP-047 ac-1 (operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR."). A unit test that checks a recorded time (an auth rotation, a selection or a session transition) takes the clock values from test-owned scripted inputs and asserts them exactly; it never compares with the current time, never sleeps to separate two times, and its result cannot change with elapsed time, scheduling delay or a change to the system clock (hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3; strengthened between rounds under the operator's "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "don't gate on me between rounds", 2026-11-03). This covers every recorded time a unit test checks, including the creation and update times a service stamps on a record it stores: the test supplies the service's clock as scripted times and asserts that each stamp equals the scripted time the service read (sibling sweep before round 11 of hostile validation round 10 finding R10-F3, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). A wall-clock bound is an assertion whose outcome depends on how much real time passes: an elapsed time compared with a limit, or work the test expects to have happened during a short real-time wait (for example a periodic tick, a file-system event or a debounce); such a test is an integration test. A timeout whose only effect is to fail a test that would otherwise hang, set far above the time the awaited step needs, is not a wall-clock bound (holistic read before round 11, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). A cancellation or timeout that a unit test arms on a real timer is such a wait when a step the test asserts must happen before the timer fires (finding of the hostile validation round 11 that stopped without a verdict, 2026-11-03, under the same rulings). Of the two sentences above, the hang-guard sentence governs: a timer a unit test arms whose only effect when it fires is to fail a test that would otherwise hang is a hang guard, not a wall-clock wait, even when an asserted step must finish before it fires. A test-armed cancellation or timeout is a wall-clock wait when its firing changes what the code under test does (for example it cancels or times out the operation whose outcome the test asserts) and an asserted step must happen before it fires. "Far above" means at least 100 times the longest real or scripted delay of the awaited step; a step with no real or scripted delay meets it for any positive timeout (holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding B4; operator 2026-11-03: "Strengthen + margin (Recommended)"). The longest real or scripted delay of the awaited step is the sum of every real or scripted delay on its path: the waits, polls and delays the test scripts and the production waits, polls and deadlines the step passes through, read from the sources, never a measured run time (third holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding d3; operator 2026-11-04: "Fix it", read as the recommended option "Strengthen + headroom"). A wait that happens only under a condition the step can meet, such as the 150 ms sleep before Microsoft.Data.Sqlite retries a statement that found the database busy, counts in that sum once for each poll on the path (fourth holistic read before hostile validation round 12, finding g1; operator 2026-11-04: "Strengthen: include them"). The same holds for every age, expiry or staleness decision a unit test checks, including one made inside the production code the test calls (for example a stale-turn query, a cleanup of old temporary files or a hygiene threshold): the test supplies the reference time as a scripted clock and the recorded times as scripted inputs, the decision is determined by those inputs alone, immediately before, at and after the threshold, and it cannot change with the system clock or the time spent between steps (hostile validation round 12 finding R12-F2; strengthened between rounds under the operator's "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "don't gate on me between rounds", 2026-11-05). This includes an age, expiry or staleness decision that a background callback in the code under test makes (for example an idle-session cleanup timer, a periodic loop or a deadline the production code arms) whenever its firing can alter a unit lifecycle assertion: the callback runs only when the test triggers it, the reference and recorded times are scripted inputs, and the same scripted trace gives the same result regardless of real elapsed time or wall-clock adjustment. An exclusion argued from how long a step takes (for example "the first tick comes after 60 s") does not meet this criterion; only an exclusion the code or the test enforces does (hostile validation round 13 finding R13-F1, proposed criterion scripted-background-expiry; strengthened between rounds under the operator's "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option" and "don't gate on me between rounds", 2026-11-06). A test that triggers such a callback asserts its decisions only after it has observed that the pass it triggered has run to its end: a decision that keeps a record is read together with an observation from the same triggered pass that only a finished pass can give (for example a record past the threshold that the same pass has already removed), so a pass that is still running, or that runs later, cannot make a keep assertion pass, and a negative control whose triggered pass finishes later is rejected (fifteenth holistic read before hostile validation round 14, finding d7; added under the operator's "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval" and "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option", 2026-11-06). Such an observation shows a finished pass only when no removal of that pass can suspend before the decision is read, and the code or the test enforces that: when a pass removes records one at a time and can await between removals, a record it has already removed shows only that the pass reached that record, so the test either reads the decision after the pass's last removal or shows that no removal in its trace can await (for example because no record in the trace holds a resource whose release awaits). A removal decision may be read directly after the trigger, because an unfinished pass can only make it fail (sixteenth holistic read before hostile validation round 14, findings e1 and g2; added under the operator's "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval" and "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option", 2026-11-06). To show that no removal in its trace can await, the test checks it at run time, in the same trace and before each trigger whose decisions it reads, from what the code under test was given or did (for example that no dependency handed it a resource whose release awaits), so that a later change that lets a removal await fails the test instead of leaving it green; a statement in the test's documentation or assertion messages alone does not show it (seventeenth holistic read before hostile validation round 14, finding g2; added under the operator's "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval" and "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option", 2026-11-06). The run-time check covers every way a removal can await, not only the kinds of resource the test knows of: after each trigger whose decisions it reads, and before it reads them, the test observes directly that the pass it triggered has finished (for example that the task of that pass has completed), so that a later change that adds any awaited step to the removal path fails the test instead of leaving it green; a check that counts only one kind of resource whose release awaits (for example agent execution sessions) does not show it (eighteenth holistic read before hostile validation round 14, finding G1; added under the operator's "if you surface new AC, add them without waiting for approval" and "Strengthening Acceptance Criteria should always be the recommended option", 2026-11-06).

The rejected fourteenth receipt is preserved with an explicit supersession notice, and the fifteenth evidence records every failed, inconclusive, and passing run with independently verified hashes and command mappings.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Linux preflight classifies each path prefix with statx(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW) and reads link targets with readlink, so a symbolic link to any path inside a userspace or network mount (not only its root) is rejected from the mount table without sending that mount a request (BUG-BASELINE-009 C1; proved by the Linux FUSE symlink integration test, which cites this criterion).

The SQLite caller-side data-source preflight runs off the caller's thread under the open's single finite deadline and the caller's cancellation: OpenAsync returns its task at once, a preflight that does not return fails the open with TimeoutException at the bound, no open worker starts, and the preflight stays counted (ActivePreflightCount) until it actually returns (BUG-BASELINE-009 C2; proved by the SQLite bounded-open preflight integration test, which cites this criterion).

Linux workspace identity resolution resolves symbolic-link prefixes through the mount table before its anchored RESOLVE_NO_XDEV lookup, so an absolute alias within a nested approved mount (for example /tmp) resolves like the data-file and SQLite opens instead of failing with a mount transition (BUG-BASELINE-009 C3; proved by the native workspace-identity resolver integration test, which cites this criterion).

A bounded traversal or file worker that uses the export root descriptor holds a reference on it from before it starts until it actually exits, so disposing the root at the public deadline defers the close: on Linux the root descriptor stays open while the worker runs and closes after it exits; on Windows the open root still blocks rename (BUG-BASELINE-009, operator decision 2026-10-11 "Fix it now"; proved by the bounded traversal integration test, which cites this criterion).

Physical workspace identity rejects safe lexical paths whose physical target is on an unsafe mount, remains safe across symlink or mount replacement timing, completes publicly within its deadline, and reports any unstoppable worker as active until it actually exits.

SQLite data-source validation and pre-handle opening resist safe-link and check-to-open replacement, use no ineffective Thread.Interrupt dependency for native Linux I/O, finish cleanup within a finite deadline, and preserve exact lifecycle, handle, worker, and exception state.

PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 57014 is translated to caller cancellation only with causal evidence produced by the caller-triggered cancellation mechanism; statement timeout and administrative cancellation remain PostgresException even during concurrent token cancellation.

A platform-specific test (TR-MCP-USECASE-018 AC-006) proves real execution and inventory counts and never passes through source inspection, skip, silent return, abort, inconclusive outcome, or a below-minimum count (operator 2026-10-30: "D3: dedupe lane rules (Recommended)"). A test fixture that needs a directory junction or link creates it with an operating-system call made in the test process, so no test outcome depends on how long a helper process takes to start (operator 2026-10-26: "Fix flake, strengthen AC (Recommended)"; at f5cda3c1 two Windows lane cases failed when a 5-second budget for starting pwsh.exe ran out under load; triage-report-8c2c30ef63d442bdb29fd785ec91e7d7). The rules this criterion shares with TR-MCP-USECASE-018 AC-006 (unit tests independent of the platform and the process environment, the lane inputs, the hostile-environment scope, no wall-clock bound in a unit test) are stated there once, and the environment-delta rule is FR-MCP-047 ac-1 (operator 2026-10-29: "Move criteria that are misplaced.  Unit tests are for FR, Integration tests are for TR.").

Containment race coverage requires at least one successful contained read and write while proving no escape or corruption, and deterministic total-rejection tests prove that rejecting every attempt cannot satisfy the success gate.

Windows descendant cleanup establishes containment at process creation or proves an equivalent race-free boundary before descendants can escape, and timeout or cancellation terminates immediate descendants finitely without regressing non-Windows process-group cleanup.

Historical rejected receipts remain intact but are explicitly superseded; final evidence identifies the exact immutable tested SHA, contains executable commands or a mechanically complete ledger, independently reconciles hashes, mappings and totals, and limits conclusions to the proven local and retained-evidence boundary.

`VoiceConversationService` manages the full voice session lifecycle: session creation with `CopilotInteractiveSession` spawned via `DesktopProcessLauncher` (or standard `Process.Start`), turn processing with tool-call loop (max `MaxToolSteps` iterations), in-memory transcript storage, tool-call record tracking, and session cleanup. Configurable via `VoiceConversationOptions` bound from `Mcp:Voice` configuration section (model, timeouts, rate limits for writes/deletes per turn, transcript context limit).
**Covered by:** `VoiceConversationService`, `VoiceConversationOptions`, `CopilotInteractiveSession`
technical.title: Voice Conversation Service

technical.body:
`VoiceController` at `/mcpserver/voice/session/*` exposes 8 endpoints: `POST /` (create session with `DeviceId`/`Language`/`ClientName`), `GET /?deviceId=` (find by device), `POST /{id}/turn` (synchronous turn), `POST /{id}/turn/stream` (SSE streaming turn), `POST /{id}/interrupt` (cancel active turn), `POST /{id}/escape` (send ESC chars to Copilot stdin), `GET /{id}` (session status), `GET /{id}/transcript` (transcript entries), `DELETE /{id}` (destroy session). DTOs: `VoiceSessionCreateRequest/Response`, `VoiceTurnRequest/Response`, `VoiceInterruptResponse`, `VoiceSessionStatusDto`, `VoiceTranscriptEntryDto/Response`, `VoiceToolCallRecordDto`, `VoiceTurnStreamEvent`.
**Covered by:** `VoiceController`, `VoiceConversationContracts`
technical.title: Voice Controller REST API

technical.body:
One active session per device enforced via `DeviceId` lookup; creating a new session for a device with an active session returns the existing session. Idle timeout (`SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes`, default 15) triggers the configured idle-shutdown prompt sent to Copilot, waits for the configured sentinel response, then terminates the session. `UseDesktopLaunch` option (default true) selects `CreateProcessAsUser` for Windows service context.
**Covered by:** `VoiceConversationService.OnIdleCleanupTick` / `CleanupIdleSessionsAsync` (60s timer-driven idle-shutdown orchestrator), `VoiceConversationOptions.SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes`, `VoiceConversationOptions.IdleShutdownCommand` (config string sent to Copilot), `VoiceConversationOptions.IdleShutdownSentinel` (config string awaited as the shutdown confirmation). Note: `IdleShutdownCommand` and `IdleShutdownSentinel` are configured strings on `VoiceConversationOptions`, not CLR message types.
technical.title: Voice Session Lifecycle Management

acceptanceCriteria.text: AC-QB-OPENS-LINKED-REQUEST-TURN-BEFORE-AGENT-WORK: Every actual user request opens a linked turn with the full request text before agent work, using a deterministic provisional title derived from the request that is never empty and never the literal User prompt; before completion the turn carries a summary title meeting completion obligation (d). TEST-QB-007: opens_linked_request_turn_before_agent_work. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-RECORDS-ORDERED-ACTIONS-AND-SEPARATE-DECISIONS: Outcomes/errors/cancellation/decisions retain status, ordering, and separate action/decision classification. tool_execution is emitted only after the server/REPL/plugin taxonomy prerequisite is verified. One explicit decision has the same identity and conclusion in designDecisions, decision dialog and design_decision action after replay; tool activity alone does not invent a decision. Out-of-order acknowledgments cannot reorder stored events or transfer a canceled/terminal turn outcome to another request. TEST-QB-008: records_ordered_actions_and_separate_decisions. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-DISTINGUISHES-CONFIRMED-AUDIT-FROM-PENDING-RECOVERY: Pending/synthetic acknowledgments are not confirmed persistence; recovery retains records and avoids duplicate application. Crash/restart at capture, pending-to-minted rebinding, submission, server commit, receipt handling and retirement retains immutable event identity, payload and per-turn order. At-least-once replay applies one logical event and never changes its request attribution. Confirmed and verified-unchanged receipts require matching root identities, event/payload and positive committed revision; duplicate requestIds and identical resubmission follow the agreed C3 outcomes. Alias recovery survives clear/restart and is not forgotten before durable consumer acknowledgment. Queued, rejected, lost, quarantined or retry-capped mandatory evidence remains visible and blocks successful completion; an empty queue cannot erase a retained rejection. TEST-QB-009: distinguishes_confirmed_audit_from_pending_recovery. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-PRESERVES-EXACT-REQUEST-AND-FINAL-RESULT-WITH-COMPLETE-TURN-COVERAGE: For every actual user request, including steering, the confirmed record preserves its complete request and final response text prepared for delivery, under the captured workspace, native session, MCP session and request identities, subject only to the existing secret policy and this operator-approved storage normalization: U+2013 and U+2014 become U+002D. Those two Unicode dash characters must not be stored; do not bypass the REPL normalization with escaping. After that policy, server readback is ordinally identical to the full expected text, preserving all other Unicode, Markdown, whitespace and newlines without trimming or summarization. A title or summary may be separate metadata but never substitutes for the response. Completion checks the expected request/event/result set, not only empty queues or equal counts. Missing, summarized, truncated, duplicated, misattributed or otherwise modified content blocks successful completion and remains visible for recovery. Cancellation without a final result does not invent one. Replay preserves one logical record and the same normalized full text. A crash after persistence but before delivery must not be represented as proof that the operator received the response. TEST cases: Both prohibited dash characters normalize to ASCII hyphens; literal and escaped input cannot retain prohibited dashes; existing ASCII hyphens and unrelated Unicode remain unchanged; exact whitespace/newline/Markdown response; same-count wrong request; summary substituted for result; omitted ingress event with zero pending counters; steering before/after response persistence; two sessions with identical text; timeout before/after server commit; crash before actual delivery; redaction identical on both output boundaries. TEST-QB-069: preserves_exact_request_and_final_result_with_complete_turn_coverage. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-ISOLATES-CLINE-QB-STATE-AND-GOVERNS-COMPATIBILITY-ENTRYPOINTS: cline-qb is an independently installed derivative application that operates without an upstream Cline installation and coexists with one when present. It uses its own isolated state root, environment names, hub endpoint and application identifiers while keeping internal wire identifiers compatible where safe; upstream ~/.cline data and upstream extension/webview storage are never read implicitly, migrated or modified, and every retained compatibility launch path is governed. cline-qb never takes ownership of, repoints, aliases as its own storage, migrates, overwrites or deletes any Cline-owned folder or data. Installation, startup, normal operation, recovery, update and uninstall leave absent upstream roots absent and seeded Cline folders, contents, ownership, permissions and link targets unchanged; Cline remains independently usable. Product isolation does not change or redirect the operator HOME or Cline paths. Before P1 closure, every inventoried host resolver and consumer must exclude upstream user roots, redirected Documents/Cline, ~/Cline/Rules and upstream extension/webview state from automatic reads, creation, migration, cleanup and uninstall. Test absent and seeded roots, constructor/webview startup, projectless fallback/import, hooks, legacy custom-instruction migration and delayed callbacks. Retain permitted governed contribution reads from shared workspace .cline/.clinerules/.agents and vendor-neutral ~/.agents, including .clinerules/workflows in both rule and workflow discovery; compatibility reads grant no ownership and do not authorize using those locations for cline-qb-owned state or rewriting their contributions. Generic SDK defaults remain compatible through host injection. P1 establishes the runtime isolation cases; P5 owns final all-host branding, compatibility and installed-artifact acceptance. TEST-QB-053: isolates_cline_qb_state_and_governs_compatibility_entrypoints. TDD stages: P1 runtime storage isolation; P5 all-host identity and installed-artifact acceptance. acceptanceCriteria.text: AC-QB-GATES-ALL-SUCCESSFUL-COMPLETION-PATHS: Successful final-answer payloads/success events remain withheld until required checks pass; blocked or incomplete diagnostics remain deliverable without claiming success. Test successful, correctable-incomplete and infrastructure-blocked outcomes through each final-delivery path. A corrected final attempt uses the same open request and only succeeds after every applicable obligation is verified; unchanged incomplete attempts stop at the existing bounded limit. Infrastructure failure exposes supported recovery without allowing ordinary work or discarding audit evidence. TEST-QB-010: gates_all_successful_completion_paths. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-BLOCKS-COMPLETION-ON-FAILED-MISSING-OR-STALE-VERIFICATION: Code/doc edits and command-made changes invalidate stale evidence; failed/missing applicable checks block completion. The signed policy selects every applicable runner from package ownership and dependency scope, including non-sdk VS Code suites, all distinct desktop runners and required native checks. Evidence binds policy digest and pre/post source fingerprints; changes during verification invalidate it. Ignored receipt churn alone does not invalidate source evidence. Baseline failures, blocked chains and required platform/credential cases remain explicit blockers until resolved or changed by an operator decision. TEST-QB-011: blocks_completion_on_failed_missing_or_stale_verification. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-CLASSIFIES-OPERATIONS-AND-GATES-PHASE-CLOSURE-ON-VERIFIED-HV-RECEIPT: A host-owned classifier derives phaseId and phaseClosing from trusted governed TODO/task mutations and MCP records, never model prose. It classifies operationClass from that trusted state plus source fingerprints: any working-tree content change within the verification-policy scope is development, whether made by an edit tool or command; administrative turns have unchanged source contents and only TODO, requirement or session-record effects. Administrative turns carry no verification or HV obligation; development turns complete only after required verification passes for the current fingerprint; a mutation completing a task or setting done: true on a TODO listed as phase-gated by the signed workspace verification policy is rejected without a valid HV receipt; for this workspace the policy lists QB-AGENT-001 tasks prefixed P1: through P5: and Final:, and done: true on QB-AGENT-001; TODOs without a phase-gate entry carry no HV obligation. The named test rejects forged reviewer/root identities, model-selected phase selectors, partial or missing verdict persistence, absent scores and every sub-98 value without rounding; it accepts valid lexical scores only under the agreed lossless numeric contract. Canonical task readback must match the attempted phase transition and current verified plan/base/head; read failure or mismatch leaves that transition pending. Administrative reconciliation never satisfies a product AC or silently closes a phase. TEST-QB-012: classifies_operations_and_gates_phase_closure_on_verified_hv_receipt (administrative, development, valid receipt, forged receipt, stale receipt). TDD: P1. Valid receipt: read back through the supported plugin from a completed MCP turn whose session agent identity is the configured reviewer identity (ClaudeCode), not the host identity; its stored verdict records OverallVerdict AGREE, accuracy and completeness >=98, and plan hash, base SHA and head SHA equal to the closing state. The host binds model-facing session tools to its own agentIdentity and sessionId; tool arguments cannot set agent, sourceType or sessionId. An administrator or unrestricted user-authorized shell with the raw marker key can bypass the application and forge server records; this on-disk credential bypass is outside the application-level guarantee and is documented as a limit under AC-QB-CHECKS-DOCUMENTED-COMMANDS-DEFAULTS-AND-CONTRACTS.

AC-QB-ISOLATES-ALL-VERIFICATION-PROCESSES-FROM-OPERATOR-APPLICATION-STATE: Every required verification fixture and its child processes use isolated application state and explicitly selected test identities, workspace, discovery endpoints and ports before application initialization. Tests must not read live operator credentials, attach to a live operator hub or change operator application state. Seeded external-state canaries and inventories remain unchanged after success, assertion failure, timeout and cancellation. Cleanup affects only resources owned by that test run. Any intentionally live integration fixture uses an explicitly provisioned test account/workspace and cannot silently inherit the operator account. Read-only compiler/package caches may be shared when they contain no operator application identity or mutable product state. TEST cases: Pre-import environment capture; account feature-flag callback; real HOME inherited by a child; parallel fixtures; wrong discovery file/port; failure and timeout cleanup; mocked negative fixture plus a real compiled positive launch; canaries outside the test root. TEST-QB-071: isolates_all_verification_processes_from_operator_application_state. TDD: P1. Staged regressions: P2, P3, P4, P5.

AC-QB-RENDERS-SESSION-LOG-AND-TODO-CONTENT-AS-INERT-DATA: Session Log and TODO content is displayed as data. ANSI/OSC/CSI sequences, HTML, scripts, remote resources and instruction-like text in server fields cannot execute code, alter terminal/window/clipboard state, initiate automatic network access, invoke a tool, mutate records or approve an action. Renderers safely represent such content while preserving the canonical value and existing explicit detail/copy security rules. This holds for summary, detail, error, loading-to-loaded updates and restored views in both TUI and desktop. TEST cases: OSC clipboard and hyperlink escapes; CSI cursor controls; HTML/script and remote image content; malformed Unicode; instruction-like text; status/error field injection; narrow live/restored views; explicit safe detail and copy. AC-QB-BOUNDS-INDIVIDUAL-RECORD-AND-DETAIL-PAYLOAD-PROCESSING: A single oversized or malformed record, detail value or streamed response cannot cause unbounded transport buffering or UI work. The slice contract defines supported byte/item limits and recoverable boundary outcomes before implementation. Supported complete data remains available without silent loss; an over-limit or malformed response is explicitly failed/stale with actionable expansion or recovery behavior and is never shown as confirmed complete truncated data. Cancellation/context change releases work and prevents late rendering under another context. Ordinary navigation and governance remain responsive. TEST cases: One huge item in a small page; exact byte limit and one over; many small items; malformed encoding; endless chunk stream; cancellation midway; repeated expansion; old-context completion; full supported data remains available. TEST-QB-076: bounds_individual_record_and_detail_payload_processing. TDD: P2. Staged regressions: P3, P4.

Failed save never advances or selects a fallback; successful explicit selection preserves its provider/model. TEST-QB-062: offers_only_compatible_direct_onboarding_forms. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-PRESERVES-EXPLICIT-SCHEDULE-PROVIDER-MODEL-SELECTION: Schedule creation requires an explicit permitted provider and model, or a previously explicit remembered pair still available in that same provider catalog. Missing provider/model blocks submission with an actionable message and no mutation. AC-QB-REQUIRES-EXPLICIT-REPLACEMENT-OF-HOSTED-SCHEDULE-SELECTION: Editing a legacy hosted schedule presents an actionable exclusion diagnostic and requires an explicit direct provider/model replacement before saving. Opening, canceling or failed validation neither activates the hosted provider nor silently rewrites the stored schedule. The replacement uses only the operator-selected permitted pair. TEST-QB-065: requires_explicit_replacement_of_hosted_schedule_selection. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-KEEPS-MIGRATED-SCHEDULE-MODEL-SELECTION-ATOMIC: When a schedule contains the structured modelSelection field, its provider/model pair is authoritative as a unit. Schedules without the structured field retain their explicit legacy direct pair. Mixed-format and partially migrated records cannot combine identities from different provider selections. TEST-QB-066: keeps_migrated_schedule_model_selection_atomic. TDD: P1.

AC-QB-REQUIRES-EXPLICIT-DIRECT-DESKTOP-RECOVERY: Desktop chat composition and recovery never fetch or subscribe to hosted feature flags, activate hosted execution from legacy state, or offer account-backed recovery links. Moving from an unavailable hosted history session to permitted execution requires an explicit new local or self-controlled remote session; it does not silently reinterpret the old session. Explicit local recovery preserves a permitted captured or remembered provider/model pair, leaves missing selection incomplete for Settings, and never chooses a hosted or first-catalog fallback. TEST-QB-067: requires_explicit_direct_desktop_recovery. TDD: P1.

AppendProcessingDialogAsync, UpsertTurnAsync, ReplaceTurnAsync and ReplaceTurnSectionAsync (with ClearTurnSectionAsync) read the turn and write its items inside one serializable transaction on a relational provider when the caller has none open, as SubmitAsync does, so writes to one turn committed at the same moment serialize or the losing one is refused with its provider's contention error (SQLite busy or locked, SQL Server deadlock 1205, PostgreSQL 40001 or 40P01), which McpErrorClassifier reports as retryable; UpsertTurnAsync's retry after a lost first insert of the same request id runs in a fresh transaction (PLAN-SESSIONTRIAGEFIX-001 A7 follow-up, triage-report-905c3ac1b6af4d57b9c24c2383642379, operator decision 2026-10-16 "Fix it in this plan").

technical.body:
Hourly, daily, and monthly USD caps SHALL be enforced server-side when dispatching. mcp-web only edits the caps. Client-side only checks are not sufficient.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-WEB-020; TEST: TEST-WEB-020

technical.body:
Workspace/agent/TODO context SHALL compose from existing template and memory APIs where they fit. New fields are allowed only when those APIs cannot represent persona text.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-WEB-007, FR-WEB-008, FR-WEB-019; TEST: TEST-WEB-007, TEST-WEB-008, TEST-WEB-019

technical.body:
TODO-to-commit mapping SHALL read session-log actions with type commit. mcp-web SHALL NOT parse git logs as the primary source.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-WEB-010, FR-WEB-015; TEST: TEST-WEB-010, TEST-WEB-015
technical.title: Commit linkage from session-log commit actions

technical.body:
Token burn and daily progress SHALL be aggregated from session-log tokenCount, commit actions, and agent-pool working timestamps. Do not scrape git independently unless session-log data is missing, and then record the fallback in the UI.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-WEB-009, FR-WEB-010; TEST: TEST-WEB-009, TEST-WEB-010

technical.body:
Start, stop, recycle, status, start-all, stop-all, and queue dispatch SHALL call /mcpserver/agent-pool via AgentPoolClient. mcp-web SHALL NOT spawn agent processes itself.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-WEB-001, FR-WEB-002, FR-WEB-003, FR-WEB-005, FR-WEB-007, FR-WEB-012, FR-WEB-014, FR-WEB-019, FR-WEB-020; TEST: TEST-WEB-001, TEST-WEB-002, TEST-WEB-003, TEST-WEB-005, TEST-WEB-007, TEST-WEB-012, TEST-WEB-014, TEST-WEB-019, TEST-WEB-020

technical.body:
The mcp-web client bundle SHALL NOT send prompt text, file bodies, or diffs to hosts other than the configured MCP Server and the operator-configured model providers used by the pool.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-WEB-016; TEST: TEST-WEB-016
technical.title: No prompt or file telemetry from mcp-web

technical.body:
If MCP Server has no recurring TODO scheduler, add a server-side scheduler that creates/reopens TODOs. mcp-web only authors the schedule fields. Browser timers SHALL NOT be the source of truth.
**Covered by:** FR: FR-WEB-006; TEST: TEST-WEB-006

technical.body:

Task bank CRUD, lanes, assignment, and dependencies SHALL use MCP TODO APIs. Direct reads or writes of TODO.yaml / docs/todo.yaml are forbidden.
